notes.ko:
**저자** 유길준(兪吉濬, 1856–1914)은 서울 출신의 개화 사상가이자 관료다. 1881년 일본(신사유람단 수행)과 1883년 미국(보빙사 수행)에서 유학하여 한국인 최초의 미국 유학생으로 꼽힌다. 1885년 귀국한 뒤 한동안 연금 상태에 있으면서 이 책을 집필했다고 전해진다. 갑오개혁(1894–96) 때 내부협판·내무대신 등을 지내며 개혁에 참여했으나, 1896년 아관파천으로 개혁 내각이 무너지자 일본으로 망명했고 1907년에야 귀국했다. 귀국 후 흥사단 등 계몽·교육 활동에 힘썼으며, 한일병합 뒤 일본의 작위 수여를 거부했다고 전해진다. 정치적으로는 군주제를 유지한 채 점진적으로 제도를 고치자는 온건 개화파로 분류되는 것이 일반적이다. 갑오개혁기에 일본에 의존한 점은 평가가 엇갈리며, 일반적으로 친일파로 분류되지는 않으나 평가에는 논란이 있다.

**시대적 맥락** 1880년대 조선은 개항과 서구 제도의 도입을 둘러싸고 개화파와 보수 세력이 맞서 있었다. 이 책은 일본·미국 체험과 서양 서적에 근거해 서양의 정치·법·교육·산업을 소개하려 한 책이다. 1895년 갑오개혁기에 출간되어, 개혁 구상과 맞닿은 개화 사상의 대표 저술로 평가된다.

**배경** 「서유견문」은 모두 20편으로, 1889년경 탈고되어 1895년 도쿄 교순사에서 간행되었다. 이 글은 제4편 「인민의 권리」다. 국한문혼용체를 처음 본격적으로 쓴 저술로 알려져 있다.

**의의** 서양의 자유·권리 개념을 한문 어휘로 옮겨 설명한 초기 시도다. 흥미롭게도 권리가 하늘이 준 것이라 하면서도 법률이 이를 보호하고 제한한다고 보아, 자연권론을 군주제 질서와 조화시키려 한다. 일본(후쿠자와 유키치 등)의 영향이 크다고 보는 연구가 많다.

**형식과 주제** 정의 → 분류 → 일곱 가지 권리(신명·재산·영업·집회·종교·언사·명예) → 법과 교육의 역할 순으로 논지를 전개한다. 핵심 개념은 자유와 통의(通義, 곧 권리), 그리고 '유계(有係)'와 '무계(無係)'의 구분이다. 마지막은 권리가 교육을 뿌리로 하고 법률이 지킨다는 결론이다.

**읽기 도움**
- 通義(통의): 권리. 오늘의 '권리'에 해당하는 개념어.
- 有係/無係(유계/무계): 타인과 관계되는 / 관계되지 않는.
- 蠻夷의 自由: 야만적 자유. 금수의 자유와 대비되는 말.
- 萬乘(만승): 천자·군주.
- -ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ(하건대), -ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니(하나니), -홈이라(함이라): 옛 어미와 명사형. 현대 철자로는 '하건대/하나니/함이라'.
- -ᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이라(따름이라): '~할 뿐이다'.
- 호ᄃᆡ/로ᄃᆡ(하되/로되): '~하되, ~이로되'.
- 야니(아니): 원문 전사의 '야니'는 '아니'의 오기로 보인다.
notes.en:
**About the author** Yu Gil-jun (兪吉濬, 1856–1914) was an enlightenment (개화) thinker and official born in Seoul. He studied in Japan in 1881 (attached to the Gentlemen's Observation Mission) and in the United States from 1883 (attached to the Korean mission), and is counted as the first Korean to study in America. After returning in 1885 he is said to have written this book while under a kind of house arrest. During the Gabo reforms (1894-96) he served as vice-minister and then minister of the interior, but when the reform cabinet fell after King Gojong took refuge in the Russian legation (1896), he fled to Japan and returned only in 1907. He then devoted himself to education and enlightenment work, and is said to have declined a Japanese title after the 1910 annexation. Politically he is generally classed as a moderate reformer who wanted gradual change under the monarchy. His reliance on Japan during the reforms is judged variously; he is not generally classed as a pro-Japanese collaborator (친일), though assessments are debated.

**Historical context** In the 1880s Joseon was divided between enlightenment reformers and conservatives over opening the ports and adopting Western institutions. The book draws on his experience in Japan and America and on Western books to introduce Western politics, law, education and industry. It appeared in 1895, in the Gabo-reform years, and is regarded as a leading statement of enlightenment thought close to the reformers' programme.

**Background** Observations on a Journey to the West has twenty books; it was reportedly finished around 1889 and published in 1895 by Kojunsha in Tokyo. This text is Book 4, "The Rights of the People." It is known as the first major work in mixed Sino-Korean script.

**Significance** An early attempt to explain Western notions of liberty and rights in Sinitic vocabulary. Interestingly, although rights are called heaven-given, the text holds that law both protects and limits them, trying to reconcile natural-rights ideas with a monarchical order. Many scholars see strong Japanese influence (e.g. Fukuzawa Yukichi).

**Form and themes** Definition, classification, seven rights (person, property, occupation, assembly, religion, speech, reputation), then the roles of law and education. Key terms are liberty (自由), tongui (通義, rightful claims, i.e. rights), and the distinction of "related" (有係) and "unrelated" (無係) claims. It concludes that rights rest on education and are guarded by law.

**Reading help**
- 通義 (tongui): rights; the book's term for what we now call 권리.
- 有係 / 無係: related to others / not related to others.
- 蠻夷의 自由: "barbarian liberty," contrasted with beasts' liberty.
- 萬乘: the ruler of a great realm.
- -ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ, -ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니, -홈이라: old endings and nominal forms; modern 하건대 / 하나니 / 함이라.
- -ᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이라: "that is all."
- 호ᄃᆡ / 로ᄃᆡ (하되 / 로되): "although, yet."
- 야니: in this transcription it appears to be an error for 아니 ("not").

paragraphs.orig: 夫人民의權利ᄂᆞᆫ其自由와通義ᄅᆞᆯ謂홈이라今其自由及通義ᄅᆞᆯ釋ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ自由ᄂᆞᆫ其心의所好ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫᄃᆡ로何事든지從ᄒᆞ야窮屈拘碍ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ思慮의無홈을謂홈이로ᄃᆡ決斷코任意放蕩ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ趣旨야니며非法縱恣ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ擧措야니오又他人의事體ᄂᆞᆫ不顧ᄒᆞ고自己의利慾을自逞ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ意思야니라乃國家의法律을敬奉ᄒᆞ고正直ᄒᆞᆫ道理로自持ᄒᆞ야自己의當行ᄒᆞᆯ人世職分으로他人을妨害ᄒᆞ지도勿ᄒᆞ며他人의妨害도勿受ᄒᆞ고其所欲爲ᄂᆞᆫ自由ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ權利며通義ᄂᆞᆫ一言으로蔽ᄒᆞ야曰當然ᄒᆞᆫ正理라今에數例ᄅᆞᆯ擧ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ假令官職을供ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ其任責을行ᄒᆞ기에相當ᄒᆞᆫ職權을保有홈이其當然ᄒᆞᆫ正理며家宅을持有ᄒᆞᆫ者가主人의名實을備存ᄒᆞ야自己의物이라稱홈이亦當然ᄒᆞᆫ正理며錢財ᄅᆞᆯ他人에게假貸ᄒᆞᆫ者가其約償ᄒᆞᆫ利息을討求홈과田土ᄅᆞᆯ他人에게假借ᄒᆞᆫ者가其收穫의分與ᄅᆞᆯ要問홈이亦且當然ᄒᆞᆫ正理니千事萬物에其當然ᄒᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ遵ᄒᆞ야固有ᄒᆞᆫ常經을勿失ᄒᆞ고相稱ᄒᆞᆫ職分을自守ᄒᆞᆷ이乃通義의權利라今此自由와通義의權利ᄂᆞᆫ普

paragraphs.en: The rights of the people are what is called their liberty (自由) and their rightful claims (通義). To explain liberty and rightful claims: liberty means having no cramped or hindered thoughts, following whatever one's heart likes in whatever matter; but it decidedly does not mean willful licence, nor lawless, unbridled conduct, nor the intention to indulge one's own appetites with no regard for the affairs of others. It means, rather, to revere the laws of the state and keep oneself upright by honest principle, neither obstructing others by the duties one rightly performs in the world nor suffering obstruction from others; what one wishes to do, one is free to do, and that is the right of liberty. Rightful claims may be summed up in a single phrase: what is proper and just. To give a few examples: that one who holds public office possesses the official powers fitting for carrying out his charge is his proper due; that one who holds a house keeps the standing of its master and calls it his own is likewise proper; that one who has lent money to another demands the interest agreed upon, and one who has lent land to another asks for his share of the harvest, is likewise proper. In the myriad affairs and things, to follow the course that is proper to each, not to lose one's inherent constant norms, and to keep the duties that fit one's station: this is the right of rightful claims. paragraphs.orig: 天率土億兆人民의同有共享ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者니各人이各其一身의權利ᄂᆞᆫ其生과俱生ᄒᆞ야不羈獨立ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ精神으로無理ᄒᆞᆫ束縛을不被ᄒᆞ고不公ᄒᆞᆫ窒碍ᄅᆞᆯ不受ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로古人이云호ᄃᆡ一身을自由ᄒᆞ야以自守홈은千萬人의通同ᄒᆞᆫ天性이니名利富貴의比ᄒᆞᆯ者아니라ᄒᆞ며又合衆國에有名ᄒᆞᆫ厚蘭吉仁氏가曰호ᄃᆡ我身의居ᄂᆞᆫ常處가無ᄒᆞ야自由의所存ᄒᆞᆫ處가則我의居라ᄒᆞ니夫自由의保存홈이實通義의功用이라通義가人身에在ᄒᆞ야天然과人爲의分別이有ᄒᆞ니天然이라謂홈은天生ᄒᆞᆫᄃᆡ로搖改홈이無홈이오人爲라謂홈은人智로以ᄒᆞ야法律을立ᄒᆞ고此ᄅᆞᆯ從ᄒᆞ야進退ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者이니와又此通義ᄅᆞᆯ詳論ᄒᆞᆷ에有係와無係의區域이存ᄒᆞ야無係의通義ᄂᆞᆫ一人의身에屬ᄒᆞ야他關係가更無ᄒᆞᆫ者며有係의通義ᄂᆞᆫ世俗에居ᄒᆞ며世人을交ᄒᆞ야互相關係ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라
paragraphs.modern: 天率土億兆人民의 同有共享하는 者니 各人이 各其一身의 權利는 其生과 俱生하여 不羈獨立하는 精神으로 無理한 束縛을 不被하고 不公한 窒碍를 不受하는 故로 古人이 云하되 一身을 自由하여 以自守함은 千萬人의 通同한 天性이니 名利富貴의 比할 者 아니라 하며 又合衆國에 有名한 厚蘭吉仁氏가 曰하되 我身의 居는 常處가 無하여 自由의 所存한 處가 則我의 居라 하니 夫自由의 保存함이 實通義의 功用이라 通義가 人身에 在하여 天然과 人爲의 分別이 有하니 天然이라 謂함은 天生한 대로 搖改함이 無함이오 人爲라 謂함은 人智로 以하여 法律을 立하고 此를 從하여 進退하는 者이니와 又此通義를 詳論함에 有係와 無係의 區域이 存하여 無係의 通義는 一人의 身에 屬하여 他關係가 更無한 者며 有係의 通義는 世俗에 居하며 世人을 交하여 互相關係하는 者라
paragraphs.en: possessed and shared by the hundreds of millions of people under all the sky and across all the land. The right that each person holds over his own person is born together with his birth; with an unbridled, independent spirit he suffers no unreasonable restraint and receives no unjust obstruction. Therefore an ancient said, 'To keep oneself free and guard oneself is the common nature of ten thousand people, and cannot be compared with fame, profit, wealth or rank'; and the renowned American Hou-ran-gil-in (厚蘭吉仁, presumably Franklin) said, 'I have no fixed dwelling; where liberty is, there is my home.' Thus the preservation of liberty is truly the function of rightful claims. Rightful claims as they exist in a person divide into the natural and the man-made: 'natural' means what is given at birth by heaven and cannot be altered; 'man-made' means that by human wisdom laws are established and one advances and withdraws in accordance with them. Further, if one discusses these rightful claims in detail, there is a distinction between the 'related' (有係) and the 'unrelated' (無係): unrelated rightful claims belong to the individual person and have no other connection with anyone; related rightful claims are those held by one who lives in the world and has dealings with others, in mutual connection.

paragraphs.orig: 若玆ᄒᆞᆫ故로無係ᄒᆞᆫ通義ᄂᆞᆫ人의天賦에屬ᄒᆞ니天下의人에何人이든지無論ᄒᆞ고世俗內에交ᄒᆞ야交際ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者와世俗外에處ᄒᆞ야獨立無伴ᄒᆞᆫ者라도可達ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ正理나然ᄒᆞ나有係ᄒᆞᆫ通義ᄂᆞᆫ其旨가略異ᄒᆞᆫ지라人爲ᄒᆞᆫ法律로迫責ᄒᆞ야人으로ᄒᆞ여곰必守홈은不可호ᄃᆡ但法律의本旨ᄂᆞᆫ人의行爲動止ᄅᆞᆯ糾正ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者인則雖各人一身의職分에ᄂᆞᆫ關係가無ᄒᆞ야도世俗交道의職分은干涉홈이可ᄒᆞᆫ者니假使今此에一人이有ᄒᆞ야其心이自暴自棄ᄒᆞ고其行이放僻奢侈호ᄃᆡ其惡이自己一身에止ᄒᆞ야治世ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ模範을犯傷홈이無ᄒᆞᆫ則法律이如何히明察ᄒᆞ든지其罪의原由ᄅᆞᆯ罰홈이不可호ᄃᆡ泥醉無厭ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ長鯨의飮을作ᄒᆞ야街路上에顚倒ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ光景을現出ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ雖其人이自己의一身을害ᄒᆞ고他人의妨害ᄅᆞᆯ不貽ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ듯ᄒᆞ나其擧動이世間에旣然公現ᄒᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ惡風을流ᄒᆞ며人心을誘ᄒᆞ야人世의一般弊端을釀成ᄒᆞ기容易ᄒᆞᆫ故로法律의權을藉ᄒᆞ야不止홈이不可ᄒᆞ니是ᄅᆞᆯ由ᄒᆞ야觀ᄒᆞᆫ則各人의當務ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ職分이其破毁홈도公私의分域이有ᄒᆞ야法律의施及ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ界限을立홈이나然ᄒᆞ나此ᄂᆞᆫ人生의職分에設譬ᄒᆞᆫ議論이니通義에至ᄒᆞ야ᄂᆞᆫ此와亦異ᄒᆞᆫ지라人生의通義ᄂᆞᆫ一人無係ᄒᆞᆫ身으로言ᄒᆞ든지世俗交際의有係ᄒᆞᆫ身으로喩ᄒᆞ든지公私의別이無ᄒᆞ고其通義ᄂᆞᆫ必其人에게屬ᄒᆞ야外物의不動ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라
paragraphs.modern: 若玆한 故로 無係한 通義는 人의 天賦에 屬하니 天下의 人에 何人이든지 無論하고 世俗內에 交하여 交際를 行하는 者와 世俗外에 處하여 獨立無伴한 者라도 可達하는 正理나 然하나 有係한 通義는 其旨가 略異한지라 人爲한 法律로 迫責하여 人으로 하여금 必守함은 不可하되 但法律의 本旨는 人의 行爲動止를 糾正하는 者인 則雖各人一身의 職分에는 關係가 無하여도 世俗交道의 職分은 干涉함이 可한 者니 假使今此에 一人이 有하여 其心이 自暴自棄하고 其行이 放僻奢侈하되 其惡이 自己一身에 止하여 治世하는 模範을 犯傷함이 無한 則法律이 如何히 明察하든지 其罪의 原由를 罰함이 不可하되 泥醉無厭하는 長鯨의 飮을 作하여 街路上에 顚倒하는 光景을 現出하는 者는 雖其人이 自己의 一身을 害하고 他人의 妨害를 不貽하는 듯하나 其擧動이 世間에 旣然公現한 時는 惡風을 流하며 人心을 誘하여 人世의 一般弊端을 釀成하기 容易한 故로 法律의 權을 藉하여 不止함이 不可하니 是를 由하여 觀한 則各人의 當務하는 職分이 其破毁함도 公私의 分域이 有하여 法律의 施及하는 界限을 立함이나 然하나 此는 人生의 職分에 設譬한 議論이니 通義에 至하여는 此와 亦異한지라 人生의 通義는 一人無係한 身으로 言하든지 世俗交際의 有係한 身으로 喩하든지 公私의 別이 無하고 其通義는 必其人에게 屬하여 外物의 不動하는 者라
paragraphs.en: Therefore unrelated rightful claims belong to a person's heaven-given endowment: whoever a person may be under heaven, it is a principle open both to those who conduct social relations within the world and to those who dwell outside it, independent and without companions. Related rightful claims, however, differ somewhat in purport. It is not permissible to compel people to observe them by man-made law; yet since the basic purpose of law is to correct people's conduct and movements, even where a matter does not touch the duty of the individual, it is permissible to interfere in the duties of social intercourse. Suppose there were a man who had given himself up to despair, whose conduct was dissolute and extravagant, but whose evil stopped with himself and did no injury to the model of an orderly age: however keen the law's insight, it may not punish the root of his offence. But one who drinks insatiably, like the drinking of a long-whale, and sprawls in a heap on the public road, though he may seem to harm only himself and cause no hindrance to others, once his behavior has been openly displayed before the world, spreads bad customs, leads people's hearts astray, and easily breeds general abuses in human society; therefore it is not permissible to leave it unchecked, and the authority of the law must be invoked. Viewed in this way, the duties each person ought to perform, and their violation too, have a public and a private sphere, and so the boundaries to which law extends are set. Yet this is an argument drawn from the duties of life; as to rightful claims it is otherwise. A person's rightful claims, whether spoken of as an isolated, unrelated individual or illustrated by one related through social intercourse, admit no distinction of public and private; they belong necessarily to that person, and are unmoved by outside things.

paragraphs.orig: 人生의無係ᄒᆞᆫ通義ᄅᆞᆯ論ᄒᆞᆫ則其箇條가雖夥ᄒᆞ나然ᄒᆞ나其綱領을先擧ᄒᆞ야名義ᄅᆞᆯ定ᄒᆞ면卽人生의天賦ᄒᆞᆫ自由라自由ᄂᆞᆫ我心의所好ᄅᆞᆯ從ᄒᆞ야事爲ᄅᆞᆯ行홈을謂홈이니其事爲ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞ기ᄂᆞᆫ天地의正理ᄅᆞᆯ從ᄒᆞ야取捨ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ外에ᄂᆞᆫ其他何等의事故가有ᄒᆞ든지秋毫라도束縛홈을不受ᄒᆞᆯ디며屈撓홈이亦無ᄒᆞᆯ디로ᄃᆡ人이旣然히世에處ᄒᆞ야人間의交際가有ᄒᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ此交際ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ由ᄒᆞ야所受ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ惠澤과裨益이亦大ᄒᆞᆫ지라此ᄅᆞᆯ償ᄒᆞ기爲ᄒᆞ야其天賦ᄒᆞᆫ一身의自由ᄅᆞᆯ如干의讓棄홈이無ᄒᆞ면不可ᄒᆞ니一身自由의一部ᄅᆞᆯ讓棄ᄒᆞ고人世의規矩ᄅᆞᆯ從順ᄒᆞ야其惠益을蒙被ᄒᆞ야彼此의交易을行홈과同ᄒᆞᆫ者라凡人이大小의分과輕重의辨을解悟ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ自己一身의私慾을從ᄒᆞ기爲ᄒᆞ야威力을妄逞홈이必無ᄒᆞ리니若一人이其意ᄅᆞᆯ自恣ᄒᆞᆫ則他人도亦各其力을逞ᄒᆞ야私慾의放情으로相爭互競ᄒᆞ야生靈의依賴ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大法이地에塗ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로處世ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ自由ᄂᆞᆫ人人이此世에處ᄒᆞ야各其人間의一人되ᄂᆞᆫ身分으로享有ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라然ᄒᆞ기天賦ᄒᆞᆫ自由에人爲ᄒᆞᆫ法을加ᄒᆞ야其本趣와大旨ᄅᆞᆯ略變ᄒᆞ야天下의普同ᄒᆞᆫ利益을謀홈이니此道로推想ᄒᆞᆫ則法律을設ᄒᆞ야人을妨害ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者의罪ᄅᆞᆯ禁制홈이其犯者一身의天賦ᄒᆞᆫ自由ᄂᆞᆫ減滅ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫᄃᆞᆺᄒᆞ나其實은處世ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ自由ᄅᆞᆯ大增홈이이니와事實의緣由가無ᄒᆞ고人民의志意ᄅᆞᆯ束縛ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ暴政이라謂홈이可ᄒᆞ니法律을設定ᄒᆞ기臨ᄒᆞ야祗愼ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ思慮ᄅᆞᆯ不加ᄒᆞᆫ則如是ᄒᆞᆫ患이不知中其端緖ᄅᆞᆯ隱伏ᄒᆞ나寅畏ᄒᆞᆫ小心으로人의權利ᄅᆞᆯ保護ᄒᆞ면人民을自由ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ域中에導歸ᄒᆞᆯ디라世界의萬國을試見ᄒᆞᆫᄃᆞᆯ法律의設홈이無ᄒᆞ고能히其人民의自由ᄅᆞᆯ保守ᄒᆞ야一國의獨立을助成ᄒᆞᆫ者가有ᄒᆞᆫ가然ᄒᆞᆫ故로政府의立法ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大要ᄂᆞᆫ人民으로ᄒᆞ여곰各其一身을自持ᄒᆞ고因ᄒᆞ야處世ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ自由ᄅᆞᆯ合成홈오로天下의普同ᄒᆞᆫ大利ᄅᆞᆯ謀ᄒᆞ기에在홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 人生의 無係한 通義를 論한 則其箇條가 雖夥하나 然하나 其綱領을 先擧하여 名義를 定하면 卽人生의 天賦한 自由라 自由는 我心의 所好를 從하여 事爲를 行함을 謂함이니 其事爲를 行하기는 天地의 正理를 從하여 取捨하는 外에는 其他何等의 事故가 有하든지 秋毫라도 束縛함을 不受할지며 屈撓함이 亦無할지로되 人이 旣然히 世에 處하여 人間의 交際가 有한 時는 此交際하는 道를 由하여 所受하는 惠澤과 裨益이 亦大한지라 此를 償하기 爲하여 其天賦한 一身의 自由를 如干의 讓棄함이 無하면 不可하니 一身自由의 一部를 讓棄하고 人世의 規矩를 從順하여 其惠益을 蒙被하여 彼此의 交易을 行함과 同한 者라 凡人이 大小의 分과 輕重의 辨을 解悟하는 者는 自己一身의 私慾을 從하기 爲하여 威力을 妄逞함이 必無하리니 若一人이 其意를 自恣한 則他人도 亦各其力을 逞하여 私慾의 放情으로 相爭互競하여 生靈의 依賴하는 大法이 地에 塗하는 故로 處世하는 自由는 人人이 此世에 處하여 各其人間의 一人되는 身分으로 享有하는 者라 然하기 天賦한 自由에 人爲한 法을 加하여 其本趣와 大旨를 略變하여 天下의 普同한 利益을 謀함이니 此道로 推想한 則法律을 設하여 人을 妨害하는 者의 罪를 禁制함이 其犯者一身의 天賦한 自由는 減滅하는 듯하나 其實은 處世하는 自由를 大增함이이니와 事實의 緣由가 無하고 人民의 志意를 束縛하는 者는 暴政이라 謂함이 可하니 法律을 設定하기 臨하여 祗愼하는 思慮를 不加한 則如是한 患이 不知中其端緖를 隱伏하나 寅畏한 小心으로 人의 權利를 保護하면 人民을 自由하는 域中에 導歸할지라 世界의 萬國을 試見한들 法律의 設함이 無하고 能히 其人民의 自由를 保守하여 一國의 獨立을 助成한 者가 有한가 然한 故로 政府의 立法하는 大要는 人民으로 하여금 各其一身을 自持하고 因하여 處世하는 自由를 合成함으로 天下의 普同한 大利를 謀하기에 在함이라
paragraphs.en: If we discuss a person's unrelated rightful claims, their articles are many, but if we first set out the main heading and fix its name, it is the liberty that heaven has endowed in human life. Liberty means acting according to what my heart likes; beyond choosing and rejecting according to the right principle of heaven and earth, whatever other circumstances there may be, one is not to be bound by the slightest thread, nor is there any bending. But once a person lives in the world and there is intercourse among people, the benefits and advantages received through that intercourse are also great, and to repay them one must give up some part of the liberty one has been endowed with; one who gave up none would not do. It is like giving up a part of one's personal liberty, submitting to the rules of the human world, and receiving its benefits, as in an exchange between two parties. A person who grasps the distinction between great and small, light and heavy, will surely not recklessly display force in order to follow his own selfish desires; for if one man indulged his will, others too would each display their strength, and with selfish appetites let loose they would contend with one another, and the great law on which living beings rely would be trodden into the dust. Therefore the liberty of living in the world is what each person enjoys in the capacity of being one among mankind in this world. And so to apply man-made law to heaven-endowed liberty, slightly altering its original bent and general drift, is to seek the common benefit of all under heaven. Reasoning along this path, when laws are set up and the offences of those who harm others are forbidden, it may seem that the heaven-endowed liberty of the offender is diminished, but in fact the liberty of living in the world is greatly increased. By contrast, whatever binds the will of the people without any factual ground may be called tyranny; if in drawing up laws one does not apply reverent care, such evil lurks, unnoticed, concealing its first threads; but if one protects people's rights with awe and caution, one will lead the people back into the realm of liberty. Look at all the countries of the world: is there any that has preserved its people's liberty and helped to build up the independence of the nation without establishing laws? Therefore the main point of a government's legislation lies in enabling the people, each to govern himself and thereby to bring about the liberty of living in the world, and so to seek the great common benefit of all under heaven.

paragraphs.orig: 此ᄅᆞᆯ因ᄒᆞ야槪觀ᄒᆞᆫ則自由와通義ᄂᆞᆫ人生의不可奪不可撓不可屈ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ權利나然ᄒᆞ나法律을恪遵ᄒᆞ야正直ᄒᆞᆫ道理로其躬을飭ᄒᆞᆫ然後에天授ᄒᆞᆫ權利ᄅᆞᆯ保有ᄒᆞ야人世의樂을享受ᄒᆞᆯ디니自己의權利ᄅᆞᆯ愛惜ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ他人의權利ᄅᆞᆯ顧護ᄒᆞ야敢히侵犯ᄒᆞ지못ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ지라萬若他人의權利ᄅᆞᆯ侵犯ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ法律의公平ᄒᆞᆫ道가是ᄅᆞᆯ必不許ᄒᆞ야其侵犯ᄒᆞᆫ分數와ᄀᆞᆺ치亦其犯者의權利ᄅᆞᆯ剝奪ᄒᆞ리니是ᄂᆞᆫ自己의手로自己의權利ᄅᆞᆯ損傷홈이오法律의威令은其自招ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ損傷을行ᄒᆞᆯᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이라然ᄒᆞᆫ故로人의權利ᄂᆞᆫ自己가自毁ᄒᆞ기前에ᄂᆞᆫ萬乘의威와萬夫의勇이라도撓奪ᄒᆞ기不能ᄒᆞ고其自毁者의權利ᄅᆞᆯ虧屈ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道ᄂᆞᆫ惟法律이其當然ᄒᆞᆫ義ᄅᆞᆯ獨有ᄒᆞ니法律의公道아니오權利의與奪을行ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ權利의竊盜라謂홈도可ᄒᆞ며讐敵이라謂홈도可ᄒᆞ나然ᄒᆞ나自由ᄅᆞᆯ過用ᄒᆞᆫ則放蕩에近ᄒᆞᆫ故로通義로操縱ᄒᆞ야其度ᄅᆞᆯ均適ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니自由ᄂᆞᆫ比ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ良馬라駕御가其道ᄅᆞᆯ若失ᄒᆞᆫ則羈靮을脫棄ᄒᆞ야斥弛ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ氣習이層生ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로通義로其羈靮을作홈이이니와駕御ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道ᄂᆞᆫ法律에在ᄒᆞ니是以로通義ᄂᆞᆫ事物의情況을隨ᄒᆞ야各人의分限이自在ᄒᆞᆫ者라學識이蒙昧ᄒᆞ야道理ᄅᆞᆯ不辨ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ人은其分限에踰越ᄒᆞ야頑悖ᄒᆞᆫ擧措도有ᄒᆞᆯ디오不及ᄒᆞ야懦殘ᄒᆞᆫ狀態도有ᄒᆞᆯ디니此ᄅᆞᆯ調和ᄒᆞ야其中을保守ᄒᆞ기ᄂᆞᆫ在上者의大責이라
paragraphs.modern: 此를 因하여 槪觀한 則自由와 通義는 人生의 不可奪不可撓不可屈하는 權利나 然하나 法律을 恪遵하여 正直한 道理로 其躬을 飭한 然後에 天授한 權利를 保有하여 人世의 樂을 享受할지니 自己의 權利를 愛惜하는 者는 他人의 權利를 顧護하여 敢히 侵犯하지 못하는지라 萬若他人의 權利를 侵犯할진대 法律의 公平한 道가 是를 必不許하여 其侵犯한 分數와 같이 亦其犯者의 權利를 剝奪하리니 是는 自己의 手로 自己의 權利를 損傷함이오 法律의 威令은 其自招하는 損傷을 行할 따름이라 然한 故로 人의 權利는 自己가 自毁하기 前에는 萬乘의 威와 萬夫의 勇이라도 撓奪하기 不能하고 其自毁者의 權利를 虧屈하는 道는 惟法律이 其當然한 義를 獨有하니 法律의 公道 아니오 權利의 與奪을 行하는 者는 權利의 竊盜라 謂함도 可하며 讐敵이라 謂함도 可하나 然하나 自由를 過用한 則放蕩에 近한 故로 通義로 操縱하여 其度를 均適하나니 自由는 比하건대 良馬라 駕御가 其道를 若失한 則羈靮을 脫棄하여 斥弛하는 氣習이 層生하는 故로 通義로 其羈靮을 作함이이니와 駕御하는 道는 法律에 在하니 是以로 通義는 事物의 情況을 隨하여 各人의 分限이 自在한 者라 學識이 蒙昧하여 道理를 不辨하는 人은 其分限에 踰越하여 頑悖한 擧措도 有할지오 不及하여 懦殘한 狀態도 有할지니 此를 調和하여 其中을 保守하기는 在上者의 大責이라
paragraphs.en: Surveying the matter on this basis: liberty and rightful claims are rights in human life that cannot be taken away, cannot be bent, cannot be subdued. Yet only after one has respectfully obeyed the law and regulated one's person by honest principle can one keep the rights that heaven has bestowed and enjoy the pleasures of the human world. One who cherishes his own rights looks after the rights of others and dares not infringe them. If one does infringe another's rights, the impartial way of the law will certainly not allow it, and in just the measure of his infringement it will strip the offender of his rights as well; this is to damage one's own rights with one's own hand, and the law's authority merely carries out the damage he has brought on himself. Therefore, before a person has destroyed them himself, his rights cannot be bent or taken from him even by the might of a ten-thousand-chariot ruler or the courage of ten thousand men; the only way to curtail the rights of one who has destroyed them himself belongs to the law alone, by right. Anyone other than the law's public way who practises the giving and taking of rights may be called a thief of rights, or an enemy. But if liberty is overused it comes close to licence, so rightful claims are used to hold the reins and keep the proper measure. Liberty is, so to speak, a good horse: if the driving goes wrong the horse throws off the bridle and a wild, unbridled temper grows; so rightful claims serve as its bridle, and the way of driving lies in the law. Thus rightful claims depend on circumstances, and each person's limits lie within them. A man whose learning is dim and who cannot distinguish right principle may overstep his limits and act stubbornly and perversely, or fall short and be timid and feeble; to harmonize these and hold to the middle way is the great duty of those in authority.

paragraphs.orig: 凡人이世에生ᄒᆞᆷ에人되ᄂᆞᆫ權利ᄂᆞᆫ賢愚貴賤貧富强弱의分別이無ᄒᆞ니此ᄂᆞᆫ世間의大公至正ᄒᆞᆫ原理라大衆이是ᄅᆞᆯ依ᄒᆞ야其性을各遂ᄒᆞ거ᄂᆞᆯ或人이謂호ᄃᆡ人의人되ᄂᆞᆫ權利ᄂᆞᆫ各其人을隨ᄒᆞ야各其一定ᄒᆞᆫ者가有ᄒᆞ다ᄒᆞ니此ᄂᆞᆫ但其一을知ᄒᆞ고其二ᄂᆞᆫ未知ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라人의生世ᄒᆞᆫ後에占有ᄒᆞᆫ地位ᄂᆞᆫ人作ᄒᆞᆫ區別이오享存ᄒᆞᆫ權利ᄂᆞᆫ天授ᄒᆞᆫ公道니人의人되ᄂᆞᆫ理ᄂᆞᆫ天子로브터匹夫에達ᄒᆞ야毫釐의差殊가本無ᄒᆞᆫ故로形貌가相同ᄒᆞ며性情이相近ᄒᆞ야大小의分은雖異ᄒᆞ나外至ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ不義無道의暴擧ᄅᆞᆯ不受홈과內存ᄒᆞᆫ好惡取捨의本心을自持홈은亦相似홈이니人을指ᄒᆞ야人이라謂ᄒᆞᆷ에誰人이曰不可리오人이天地間에生ᄒᆞ야各其人되ᄂᆞᆫ理로視ᄒᆞ면人上人도無ᄒᆞ고人下人도無ᄒᆞ니天子도人이오匹夫도亦人이로ᄃᆡ天子라謂홈과匹夫라謂홈이人世의法律大紀로乃地位의區別을立홈인則此ᄅᆞᆯ遵照ᄒᆞ야其次序의設行홈으로地位의等分이各其占有ᄒᆞᆫ層度로名號가附成ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니尊貴卑賤의階級이始分홈이라然則地位도其當然ᄒᆞᆫ通義가自有ᄒᆞᆯ디니其權利의無홈이奈何로其可ᄒᆞ리오然ᄒᆞ기地位의權利가各其大小의差異ᄅᆞᆯ因ᄒᆞ야其適度의配合이有홈이로ᄃᆡ人의人되ᄂᆞᆫ權利와ᄂᆞᆫ不同ᄒᆞ야高下의秩序와大小의境遇ᄅᆞᆯ定ᄒᆞ고形勢의變遷得喪을由ᄒᆞ야推移有無ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者니名은實의賓이라其倘來와倘去로人生의權利에增減ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ關係ᄅᆞᆯ不生ᄒᆞ야有ᄒᆞ야도亦可ᄒᆞ고無ᄒᆞ야도亦可ᄒᆞ나人이此世에居ᄒᆞ야其占有ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ地位ᄂᆞᆫ無홈이亦不可ᄒᆞᆫ則富貴ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ富貴ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞ고貧賤ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ貧賤을行ᄒᆞ야各其地位의權利ᄅᆞᆯ遵依홈이니是故로人生의權利와地位의權利ᄅᆞᆯ二種에分ᄒᆞᆫ則其輕重이懸殊ᄒᆞ야其一은曰內有ᄒᆞᆫ眞理며其二ᄂᆞᆫ曰外來ᄒᆞᆫ勢力이라今古의人事ᄅᆞᆯ推究ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ勢力을善用ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ同類의眞理ᄅᆞᆯ保護ᄒᆞ고濫行ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ同類의眞理ᄅᆞᆯ虧傷ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니生民의休戚憂樂과有國의安危存亡이其實은此中에存홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 凡人이 世에 生함에 人되는 權利는 賢愚貴賤貧富强弱의 分別이 無하니 此는 世間의 大公至正한 原理라 大衆이 是를 依하여 其性을 各遂하거늘 或人이 謂하되 人의 人되는 權利는 各其人을 隨하여 各其一定한 者가 有하다 하니 此는 但其一을 知하고 其二는 未知하는 者라 人의 生世한 後에 占有한 地位는 人作한 區別이오 享存한 權利는 天授한 公道니 人의 人되는 理는 天子로부터 匹夫에 達하여 毫釐의 差殊가 本無한 故로 形貌가 相同하며 性情이 相近하여 大小의 分은 雖異하나 外至하는 不義無道의 暴擧를 不受함과 內存한 好惡取捨의 本心을 自持함은 亦相似함이니 人을 指하여 人이라 謂함에 誰人이 曰不可리오 人이 天地間에 生하여 各其人되는 理로 視하면 人上人도 無하고 人下人도 無하니 天子도 人이오 匹夫도 亦人이로되 天子라 謂함과 匹夫라 謂함이 人世의 法律大紀로 乃地位의 區別을 立함인 則此를 遵照하여 其次序의 設行함으로 地位의 等分이 各其占有한 層度로 名號가 附成하나니 尊貴卑賤의 階級이 始分함이라 然則地位도 其當然한 通義가 自有할지니 其權利의 無함이 奈何로 其可하리오 然하기 地位의 權利가 各其大小의 差異를 因하여 其適度의 配合이 有함이로되 人의 人되는 權利와는 不同하여 高下의 秩序와 大小의 境遇를 定하고 形勢의 變遷得喪을 由하여 推移有無하는 者니 名은 實의 賓이라 其倘來와 倘去로 人生의 權利에 增減하는 關係를 不生하여 有하여도 亦可하고 無하여도 亦可하나 人이 此世에 居하여 其占有하는 地位는 無함이 亦不可한 則富貴한 者는 富貴를 行하고 貧賤한 者는 貧賤을 行하여 各其地位의 權利를 遵依함이니 是故로 人生의 權利와 地位의 權利를 二種에 分한 則其輕重이 懸殊하여 其一은 曰內有한 眞理며 其二는 曰外來한 勢力이라 今古의 人事를 推究하건대 勢力을 善用하는 者는 同類의 眞理를 保護하고 濫行하는 者는 同類의 眞理를 虧傷하나니 生民의 休戚憂樂과 有國의 安危存亡이 其實은 此中에 存함이라
paragraphs.en: When people are born into the world, the right of being a human being admits no distinction of wise or foolish, noble or base, poor or rich, strong or weak; this is the great, impartial and perfectly just principle of the world, and on this the multitude each fulfil their nature. Some say that the right of being human differs for each person and is fixed for each; but this knows the one point and not the second. The position a person occupies after being born into the world is a distinction made by men, whereas the rights he enjoys are a public way bestowed by heaven. The principle of being human extends from the Son of Heaven down to the common man without the slightest difference: their appearance is alike and their natures are close; although the distinction of great and small differs, they are similar in not suffering the outrage of injustice and lawlessness coming from outside, and in holding to the original heart of liking and disliking, taking and leaving, within. If one points at a man and calls him a man, who would say it is wrong? Viewed by the principle by which each is a human being between heaven and earth, there is no man above men and no man below men; the Son of Heaven is a man and the common man is also a man. Yet to speak of 'Son of Heaven' and 'common man' is where, by the great rules of the law of the human world, distinctions of position are established; following this, and putting the order into effect, titles are attached according to the grade each position occupies, and so the ranks of noble and humble begin to be distinguished. Position therefore has its own proper rightful claims, and how could it be right that it should lack rights? But the rights of position differ in size according to each, and have their suitable matching; they differ from the right of being human in that they fix high and low, the order of great and small, and the circumstances, and shift, present or absent, with the changes, gains and losses of fortune. Names are the guests of reality: as they come by chance and go by chance they cause no increase or decrease in the rights of human life; having them is acceptable, and lacking them is acceptable. But since a person living in this world cannot do without some position, the rich and noble act as the rich and noble, and the poor and humble act as the poor and humble, each complying with the rights of his own position. Therefore if one divides rights into the rights of human life and the rights of position, their weights differ greatly: the first is called the truth that lies within, the second the force that comes from without. Examining human affairs past and present, those who use force well protect the truth of their fellows, and those who abuse it injure the truth of their fellows; the weal and woe, grief and joy of the people, and the safety or peril, survival or ruin of a state, in fact reside in this.

paragraphs.orig: 或人이云호ᄃᆡ人의强弱은是非로判ᄒᆞ고禽獸의强弱은勢力으로定ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로若人의强弱을是非로不判ᄒᆞ고勢力으로以ᄒᆞᆫ則是ᄂᆞᆫ禽獸의道와無異ᄒᆞ다ᄒᆞ니此言이誠然ᄒᆞ도다天地의理氣ᄅᆞᆯ受ᄒᆞ야生物의自由ᄅᆞᆯ得홈은人과禽獸의同然ᄒᆞᆫ者로ᄃᆡ禽獸ᄂᆞᆫ其自由ᄅᆞᆯ用홈에通義의覊靮이無ᄒᆞ며法律의駕御가亦無ᄒᆞ야弱의肉을强이是食ᄒᆞ야其勢力을縱恣홈으로其相生ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ作ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이오人은其相與ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ際에法律의綱紀ᄅᆞᆯ立ᄒᆞ며通義의界域을定ᄒᆞ야其自由ᄅᆞᆯ宰制ᄒᆞ며操縱홈으로人間의不齊ᄒᆞᆫ景況을調平ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니然ᄒᆞ기蠻夷의人이라도其任用ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ自由가禽獸의比類ᄒᆞᆯ배아니로ᄃᆡ盡美極善ᄒᆞᆫ境에未達ᄒᆞᆫ故로此ᄅᆞᆯ謂ᄒᆞ야蠻夷의自由라홈이라人이萬若禽獸의自由ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞ면天下에倫彝의大綢이崩壞ᄒᆞᆯ디오名義의達道가紊亂ᄒᆞᆯ디니人類의生養이何恃ᄒᆞ야保ᄒᆞ며何賴ᄒᆞ야安ᄒᆞ리오故로曰有識人의自由ᄂᆞᆫ不自由ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ中에在ᄒᆞ다ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니此ᄂᆞᆫ人慾을遏ᄒᆞ고天理ᄅᆞᆯ存ᄒᆞ야正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로其權利ᄅᆞᆯ持守홈을謂홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 或人이 云하되 人의 强弱은 是非로 判하고 禽獸의 强弱은 勢力으로 定하는 故로 若人의 强弱을 是非로 不判하고 勢力으로 以한 則是는 禽獸의 道와 無異하다 하니 此言이 誠然하도다 天地의 理氣를 受하여 生物의 自由를 得함은 人과 禽獸의 同然한 者로되 禽獸는 其自由를 用함에 通義의 覊靮이 無하며 法律의 駕御가 亦無하여 弱의 肉을 强이 是食하여 其勢力을 縱恣함으로 其相生하는 道를 作하는 따름이오 人은 其相與하는 際에 法律의 綱紀를 立하며 通義의 界域을 定하여 其自由를 宰制하며 操縱함으로 人間의 不齊한 景況을 調平하나니 然하기 蠻夷의 人이라도 其任用하는 自由가 禽獸의 比類할 배 아니로되 盡美極善한 境에 未達한 故로 此를 謂하여 蠻夷의 自由라 함이라 人이 萬若禽獸의 自由를 行하면 天下에 倫彝의 大綢이 崩壞할지오 名義의 達道가 紊亂할지니 人類의 生養이 何恃하여 保하며 何賴하여 安하리오 故로 曰有識人의 自由는 不自由하는 中에 在하다 하나니 此는 人慾을 遏하고 天理를 存하여 正直한 道로 其權利를 持守함을 謂함이라
paragraphs.en: Someone says: 'Among men strength and weakness are judged by right and wrong, but among birds and beasts they are decided by force; so if men's strength and weakness were judged not by right and wrong but by force, this would be no different from the way of birds and beasts.' This saying is indeed true. Receiving the vital breath of heaven and earth and obtaining the liberty of living creatures is the same for men and for birds and beasts; but beasts, in using their liberty, have no bridle of rightful claims and no driving of law, so the strong eat the flesh of the weak and indulge their force, and this is merely the way in which they live on one another. Men, in their dealings with one another, set up the framework of law and fix the bounds of rightful claims, and thereby govern and rein in their liberty and level out the unequal conditions among them. Even so, the liberty a barbarian exercises is not comparable to that of beasts, but because it has not reached the realm of perfect goodness it is called 'barbarian liberty.' If men were to practise the liberty of beasts, the great bonds of human relations under heaven would collapse and the universal way of names and duties would fall into disorder; what could the nurturing of mankind rely on to be preserved, or depend on to be at peace? Hence it is said that the liberty of the knowing person lies in what is unfree: that is, restraining human desire, preserving the principle of heaven, and holding to one's rights by the upright way.

paragraphs.orig: 却夫通義와自由ᄂᆞᆫ其條目을立ᄒᆞ기極難ᄒᆞ나猶且人間의事物을因ᄒᆞ야其顯明ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄅᆞᆯ略擧ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ
paragraphs.modern: 却夫通義와 自由는 其條目을 立하기 極難하나 猶且人間의 事物을 因하여 其顯明한 者를 略擧하건대
paragraphs.en: Now, it is extremely difficult to set out the articles of rightful claims and liberty one by one; yet, following the affairs and things of human life, let me briefly list the clearest of them.

paragraphs.orig: 一曰身命의自由及通義니此ᄂᆞᆫ謂호ᄃᆡ身命의權利라身命의自由ᄂᆞᆫ正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로其行動과擧止ᄅᆞᆯ操飭ᄒᆞ야自己의分限을不踰ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ拘碍도無ᄒᆞ며束縛도無ᄒᆞ야自主ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ樂을享有홈이오身命의通義ᄂᆞᆫ自己의生命과肢體ᄅᆞᆯ正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로保守ᄒᆞ야他人의妨害ᄅᆞᆯ備禦ᄒᆞ며不法의侵凌을抗避ᄒᆞ야健康安樂ᄒᆞᆫ景像을護持홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 一曰身命의 自由及通義니 此는 謂하되 身命의 權利라 身命의 自由는 正直한 道로 其行動과 擧止를 操飭하여 自己의 分限을 不踰하는 時는 拘碍도 無하며 束縛도 無하여 自主하는 樂을 享有함이오 身命의 通義는 自己의 生命과 肢體를 正直한 道로 保守하여 他人의 妨害를 備禦하며 不法의 侵凌을 抗避하여 健康安樂한 景像을 護持함이라
paragraphs.en: First: liberty and rightful claims of the person (身命). This is called the right of the person. Liberty of the person means that, so long as one regulates one's movements and conduct by the upright way and does not overstep one's own limits, there is no hindrance and no binding, and one enjoys the pleasure of being one's own master. The rightful claim of the person means that one guards one's own life and limbs by the upright way, defends against the harm of others, resists and avoids unlawful encroachment, and so maintains a state of health and ease.

paragraphs.orig: 二曰財産의自由及通義니此ᄂᆞᆫ謂호ᄃᆡ財産의權利라財産의自由ᄂᆞᆫ各人이其私有ᄒᆞᆫ財産을行用홈과處寘홈에正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로以ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ禁制ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者도無ᄒᆞ며操縱ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者도無ᄒᆞ야其自便ᄒᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ任從홈이오財産의通義ᄂᆞᆫ自己의持有ᄒᆞᆫ財産을護守ᄒᆞ야無理ᄒᆞᆫ橫奪을不受ᄒᆞ고獨操ᄒᆞᆫ實勢ᄅᆞᆯ保存홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 二曰財産의 自由及通義니 此는 謂하되 財産의 權利라 財産의 自由는 各人이 其私有한 財産을 行用함과 處寘함에 正直한 道로 以하는 時는 禁制하는 者도 無하며 操縱하는 者도 無하여 其自便한 道를 任從함이오 財産의 通義는 自己의 持有한 財産을 護守하여 無理한 橫奪을 不受하고 獨操한 實勢를 保存함이라
paragraphs.en: Second: liberty and rightful claims of property (財産). This is called the right of property. Liberty of property means that when each person uses and disposes of the property he privately owns by the upright way, no one forbids or controls him, and he follows whatever course suits him. The rightful claim of property means that one guards the property one holds, suffers no unreasonable seizure, and preserves the real power one holds alone.

paragraphs.orig: 三曰營業의自由及通義니此ᄂᆞᆫ謂호ᄃᆡ營業의權利라營業의自由ᄂᆞᆫ如何ᄒᆞᆫ事物을從ᄒᆞ야其生業을營求ᄒᆞ든지正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로行ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ樂爲ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者에任就ᄒᆞ야妨碍禁抑을不受홈이오營業의通義ᄂᆞᆫ其營求ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ生業에行用ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ事務ᄂᆞᆫ明的ᄒᆞᆫ分度ᄅᆞᆯ遵守ᄒᆞ고窮屈ᄒᆞᆫ弊害와詐僞ᄒᆞᆫ冒蔽ᄅᆞᆯ防守홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 三曰營業의 自由及通義니 此는 謂하되 營業의 權利라 營業의 自由는 如何한 事物을 從하여 其生業을 營求하든지 正直한 道로 行하는 時는 樂爲하는 者에 任就하여 妨碍禁抑을 不受함이오 營業의 通義는 其營求하는 生業에 行用하는 事務는 明的한 分度를 遵守하고 窮屈한 弊害와 詐僞한 冒蔽를 防守함이라
paragraphs.en: Third: liberty and rightful claims of occupation (營業). This is called the right of occupation. Liberty of occupation means that, whatever pursuit one follows to make one's living, so long as one acts by the upright way one takes up what one gladly does and suffers no obstruction or suppression. The rightful claim of occupation means that in the business one carries on in the trade one pursues, one observes clear limits and guards against cramping abuses and fraudulent concealment.

paragraphs.orig: 四曰集會의自由及通義니此ᄂᆞᆫ謂호ᄃᆡ集會의權利라集會의自由ᄂᆞᆫ衆人이合意ᄒᆞ야如何ᄒᆞᆫ集會ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞ든지正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로自執ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ禁抑ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者도無ᄒᆞ며妨碍ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者도無ᄒᆞ야其交好ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ樂事ᄅᆞᆯ保有홈이오集會의通義ᄂᆞᆫ其集會의規制와事務가如何ᄒᆞᆫ基礎에構成ᄒᆞ든지正直ᄒᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ不失ᄒᆞᆫ則他人의壅遏을不被ᄒᆞ고維持ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ約束을固守ᄒᆞ야其集會의特例ᄅᆞᆯ護存홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 四曰集會의 自由及通義니 此는 謂하되 集會의 權利라 集會의 自由는 衆人이 合意하여 如何한 集會를 行하든지 正直한 道로 自執하는 時는 禁抑하는 者도 無하며 妨碍하는 者도 無하여 其交好하는 樂事를 保有함이오 集會의 通義는 其集會의 規制와 事務가 如何한 基礎에 構成하든지 正直한 道를 不失한 則他人의 壅遏을 不被하고 維持하는 約束을 固守하여 其集會의 特例를 護存함이라
paragraphs.en: Fourth: liberty and rightful claims of assembly (集會). This is called the right of assembly. Liberty of assembly means that when many people agree and hold any kind of gathering, so long as they conduct it by the upright way, no one prohibits or hinders them, and they keep the pleasure of friendly fellowship. The rightful claim of assembly means that, whatever foundation the gathering's regulations and business are built on, so long as it does not lose the upright way, it suffers no blocking by others, firmly keeps the agreements that hold it together, and preserves the particular rules of the gathering.

paragraphs.orig: 五曰宗敎의自由及通義니此ᄂᆞᆫ謂호ᄃᆡ宗敎의權利라宗敎의自由ᄂᆞᆫ各人이敎ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ바와宗ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ바에一切其心悅ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄅᆞᆯ隨ᄒᆞ고禁遏拘碍ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ勒制ᄅᆞᆯ不被ᄒᆞ야綽裕ᄒᆞᆫ樂地에任歸홈이오宗敎의通義ᄂᆞᆫ歸依ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ黨徒ᄅᆞᆯ受ᄒᆞ며維持ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ規則을設ᄒᆞ기에國法의大紀ᄅᆞᆯ不背ᄒᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ其行用ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ諸般事務가自主ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ掌握에在ᄒᆞ야他人의操縱을不受홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 五曰宗敎의 自由及通義니 此는 謂하되 宗敎의 權利라 宗敎의 自由는 各人이 敎하는 바와 宗하는 바에 一切其心悅하는 者를 隨하고 禁遏拘碍하는 勒制를 不被하여 綽裕한 樂地에 任歸함이오 宗敎의 通義는 歸依하는 黨徒를 受하며 維持하는 規則을 設하기에 國法의 大紀를 不背한 時는 其行用하는 諸般事務가 自主하는 掌握에 在하여 他人의 操縱을 不受함이라
paragraphs.en: Fifth: liberty and rightful claims of religion (宗敎). This is called the right of religion. Liberty of religion means that each person follows whatever his heart delights in with regard to what he teaches and what he reveres, suffers no forcible restraint that forbids or hinders him, and is free to go to a place of ample ease. The rightful claim of religion means that, in receiving adherents and drawing up rules to sustain the body, so long as it does not run counter to the great norms of the state's law, the conduct of its various affairs lies in the hands of its own masters and is not controlled by others.

paragraphs.orig: 六曰言詞의自由니各人이上下相與ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ際에其言詞의發홈이實事ᄅᆞᆯ從ᄒᆞ고虛謂가無ᄒᆞᆫ則自主ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ權利가有홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 六曰言詞의 自由니 各人이 上下相與하는 際에 其言詞의 發함이 實事를 從하고 虛謂가 無한 則自主하는 權利가 有함이라
paragraphs.en: Sixth: liberty of speech (言詞). It means that when people speak with one another, high and low, if what they say follows the facts and contains no falsehood, they have the right to act on their own authority.

paragraphs.orig: 七曰名譽의通義니此ᄂᆞᆫ無禮ᄒᆞᆫ誹謗과不實ᄒᆞᆫ毁訾ᄅᆞᆯ防備ᄒᆞ야其聲名을保守ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ權利라
paragraphs.modern: 七曰名譽의 通義니 此는 無禮한 誹謗과 不實한 毁訾를 防備하여 其聲名을 保守하는 權利라
paragraphs.en: Seventh: the rightful claim of reputation (名譽). This is the right to guard one's good name by defending against discourteous slander and false defamation.

paragraphs.orig: 今此臚陳ᄒᆞᆫ諸條ᄂᆞᆫ其大槪ᄅᆞᆯ說出홈이니大抵人의權利ᄂᆞᆫ無雙ᄒᆞᆫ至寶나然이나各人一身의無係홈으로其天然홈을縱恣ᄒᆞᆫ則禽獸의自由와同歸ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로有係ᄒᆞᆫ通義의酌斟으로其過用ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ弊ᄅᆞᆯ限制호ᄃᆡ猶且蠻夷의自由에相近ᄒᆞᆫ故로法律의規度ᄅᆞᆯ立ᄒᆞ야生世人의自由ᄅᆞᆯ潤色홈이니然ᄒᆞᆫ則處世ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ權利ᄅᆞᆯ欲保ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ法律을敬奉ᄒᆞ야大衆의相生ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ公道ᄅᆞᆯ守홈이라法律의本意ᄂᆞᆫ人의權利ᄅᆞᆯ愼重ᄒᆞ고又因ᄒᆞ야是ᄅᆞᆯ保護ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니法律의設施가無ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ權利도其能存홈이必難ᄒᆞᆯ디라此ᄅᆞᆯ由ᄒᆞ야者ᄒᆞ면權利가雖天下人人의自有ᄒᆞᆫ至寶라ᄒᆞ나其實은法律에附依ᄒᆞ야其現像을保홈이니人의權利ᄂᆞᆫ法律의所賜라謂ᄒᆞ야도謬評이야니라法律은帥며權利ᄂᆞᆫ卒徒니卒徒가帥의命令과節制ᄅᆞᆯ不遵ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ卒徒의本分을不守ᄒᆞᆫ다謂ᄒᆞᆯ디나然ᄒᆞ나帥가萬若苛酷ᄒᆞᆫ紀律과暴虐ᄒᆞᆫ規例로卒徒의本分을抑遏ᄒᆞᆫ則亦良帥라謂ᄒᆞ기不可ᄒᆞᆯ디니此理ᄅᆞᆯ細究ᄒᆞ면法律과權利의相濟ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ關係ᄅᆞᆯ覷得ᄒᆞᆯ디로ᄃᆡ法律은權利ᄅᆞᆯ保護ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故ᄂᆞᆫ亦剝奪ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ勢와停止ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ力이有ᄒᆞ니天下의何邦에居ᄒᆞ든지其邦家의法律을不敬ᄒᆞ고能히其身의權利ᄅᆞᆯ保存ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者가未有홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 今此臚陳한 諸條는 其大槪를 說出함이니 大抵人의 權利는 無雙한 至寶나 然이나 各人一身의 無係함으로 其天然함을 縱恣한 則禽獸의 自由와 同歸하는 故로 有係한 通義의 酌斟으로 其過用하는 弊를 限制하되 猶且蠻夷의 自由에 相近한 故로 法律의 規度를 立하여 生世人의 自由를 潤色함이니 然한 則處世하는 權利를 欲保하는 者는 法律을 敬奉하여 大衆의 相生하는 公道를 守함이라 法律의 本意는 人의 權利를 愼重하고 又因하여 是를 保護하나니 法律의 設施가 無할진대 權利도 其能存함이 必難할지라 此를 由하여 者하면 權利가 雖天下人人의 自有한 至寶라 하나 其實은 法律에 附依하여 其現像을 保함이니 人의 權利는 法律의 所賜라 謂하여도 謬評이 아니라 法律은 帥며 權利는 卒徒니 卒徒가 帥의 命令과 節制를 不遵할진대 卒徒의 本分을 不守한다 謂할지나 然하나 帥가 萬若苛酷한 紀律과 暴虐한 規例로 卒徒의 本分을 抑遏한 則亦良帥라 謂하기 不可할지니 此理를 細究하면 法律과 權利의 相濟하는 關係를 覷得할지로되 法律은 權利를 保護하는 故는 亦剝奪하는 勢와 停止하는 力이 有하니 天下의 何邦에 居하든지 其邦家의 法律을 不敬하고 能히 其身의 權利를 保存하는 者가 未有함이라
paragraphs.en: These articles, now laid out in order, set out only the general outline. In sum, a person's rights are an unmatched treasure; but if each person, because he is unrelated to others, gives free rein to his natural state, he ends up with the liberty of beasts, so the abuse of overuse is limited by weighing related rightful claims; and since that still comes close to barbarian liberty, the standards of law are established to refine the liberty of those living in the world. Accordingly, one who wishes to preserve his rights in the world respectfully obeys the law and keeps the public way by which the multitude live together. The original intention of the law is to treat people's rights with gravity and, on that account, to protect them; without the application of law it would surely be difficult for rights to survive. Seen in this way, although rights are a treasure each person under heaven holds of himself, in fact they rest on the law for the preservation of their appearance, and it is no mistaken judgement to say that people's rights are bestowed by law. The law is the commander and rights are the soldiers: if the soldiers do not obey the commander's orders and discipline they may be said not to keep their duty as soldiers; but if the commander suppresses the soldiers' duty with harsh discipline and cruel rules, he too cannot be called a good commander. If one examines this principle closely one can see how law and rights complete each other. But because law protects rights, it also has the power to strip them away and to suspend them; in whatever country under heaven a man dwells, there has never been one who preserved his own rights without respecting the laws of that country.

paragraphs.orig: 身命의權利ᄅᆞᆯ論ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ人生의重大ᄒᆞᆫ天授正理라生命及肢體ᄅᆞᆯ保護ᄒᆞ야安寧健康ᄒᆞᆫ福을享受홈은人間의快樂이니不法ᄒᆞᆫ擧措로人의一髮一指라도害傷ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ天然ᄒᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ背戾홈인故로亦人에게此事ᄅᆞᆯ受홈도不可ᄒᆞᆫ지라此權利ᄂᆞᆫ其生에俱來ᄒᆞ야其死에同歸ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니死亦二種에分ᄒᆞ야一曰天然死며一曰世俗死라天然死ᄂᆞᆫ病化ᄅᆞᆯ謂홈이어니와世俗死ᄂᆞᆫ外國에徙籍홈을指홈이니然홈으로天然生은他人의力으로害홈도不可ᄒᆞ고自己의手로害홈도亦不可ᄒᆞ야惟極惡大罪로人世의法律을毁破ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ法으로其人의生命을奪ᄒᆞᆯᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이로ᄃᆡ蓋人이人을殺홈은不得已ᄒᆞᆫ事로不忍ᄒᆞᆫ政을行홈이라萬乘의威로도法으로人을刑ᄒᆞ기外에ᄂᆞᆫ他道가更無ᄒᆞ야不犯ᄒᆞᆫ人은其毫髮이라도搖動ᄒᆞ기不能ᄒᆞ니此ᄅᆞᆯ由ᄒᆞ야言ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ人이人을刑殺ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ權이無ᄒᆞ고乃法이其權을有홈인則刑ᄒᆞ든지殺ᄒᆞ든지皆法이라是以로其人이其罪ᄅᆞᆯ犯ᄒᆞ야其法을受홈이可ᄒᆞᆫ然後에執法ᄒᆞᆫ者가法의指揮ᄅᆞᆯ聽從ᄒᆞ야施行ᄒᆞᆯᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이니但法官의私意로人을欲制ᄒᆞ야도國律의不許ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ바ᄂᆞᆫ恣行ᄒᆞ기不能ᄒᆞᆯ디며設使得行ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ此ᄂᆞᆫ人의力으로人의權利ᄅᆞᆯ妨害홈이라法律의公道ᄅᆞᆯ壞ᄒᆞ야人世의大弊ᄅᆞᆯ起홈이니誰人이曰可라ᄒᆞ리오夫人身은正直홈으로自重ᄒᆞ고公平홈으로自寬홈이可ᄒᆞᆫ者라然ᄒᆞᆫ故로人의意ᄅᆞᆯ抑遏ᄒᆞ야廣厦上에寘ᄒᆞ고膏粱으로食ᄒᆞ며錦繡로衣ᄒᆞ야도此ᄂᆞᆫ拘囚홈이며道路上에人의行을勒止ᄒᆞ야도亦拘囚홈과無異홈이니身命의權利ᄂᆞᆫ國法을不犯ᄒᆞᆫ時에其自在홈을任寘홈과外來ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ傷害ᄅᆞᆯ防備홈에在ᄒᆞᆯᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이라
paragraphs.modern: 身命의 權利를 論하건대 人生의 重大한 天授正理라 生命及肢體를 保護하여 安寧健康한 福을 享受함은 人間의 快樂이니 不法한 擧措로 人의 一髮一指라도 害傷하는 者는 天然한 道를 背戾함인 故로 亦人에게 此事를 受함도 不可한지라 此權利는 其生에 俱來하여 其死에 同歸하나니 死亦二種에 分하여 一曰天然死며 一曰世俗死라 天然死는 病化를 謂함이어니와 世俗死는 外國에 徙籍함을 指함이니 然함으로 天然生은 他人의 力으로 害함도 不可하고 自己의 手로 害함도 亦不可하여 惟極惡大罪로 人世의 法律을 毁破한 者는 法으로 其人의 生命을 奪할 따름이로되 蓋人이 人을 殺함은 不得已한 事로 不忍한 政을 行함이라 萬乘의 威로도 法으로 人을 刑하기 外에는 他道가 更無하여 不犯한 人은 其毫髮이라도 搖動하기 不能하니 此를 由하여 言하건대 人이 人을 刑殺하는 權이 無하고 乃法이 其權을 有함인 則刑하든지 殺하든지 皆法이라 是以로 其人이 其罪를 犯하여 其法을 受함이 可한 然後에 執法한 者가 法의 指揮를 聽從하여 施行할 따름이니 但法官의 私意로 人을 欲制하여도 國律의 不許하는 바는 恣行하기 不能할지며 設使得行할진대 此는 人의 力으로 人의 權利를 妨害함이라 法律의 公道를 壞하여 人世의 大弊를 起함이니 誰人이 曰可라 하리오 夫人身은 正直함으로 自重하고 公平함으로 自寬함이 可한 者라 然한 故로 人의 意를 抑遏하여 廣厦上에 寘하고 膏粱으로 食하며 錦繡로 衣하여도 此는 拘囚함이며 道路上에 人의 行을 勒止하여도 亦拘囚함과 無異함이니 身命의 權利는 國法을 不犯한 時에 其自在함을 任寘함과 外來하는 傷害를 防備함에 在할 따름이라
paragraphs.en: As for the right of the person: it is a heaven-given and weighty principle of human life. To protect life and limbs and to enjoy the blessing of peace and health is the pleasure of human existence; one who with unlawful conduct injures even a hair or a finger of another goes against the natural way, and so one must not suffer such treatment from others either. This right comes into being with one's life and returns with one's death together with it; death too divides into two kinds, natural death and worldly death. Natural death means transformation by illness; worldly death means moving one's registry to a foreign country. Thus natural life may not be harmed by another's power, nor may one harm it with one's own hand; only one who has committed a most heinous crime and broken the laws of the human world may have his life taken by law. For one man to kill another is an unavoidable matter, a harsh act of government that one can scarcely bear to carry out; even a ruler of a ten-thousand-chariot realm has no way other than punishing a man by law, and cannot disturb a hair of one who has not offended. Speaking from this, men have no authority to punish and kill men; rather the law holds that authority, so whether one punishes or kills, it is all the law. Therefore only after that man has committed his crime and it is right that he receive that law may the executor of the law, following the law's directions, carry it out; but even if a judge wishes to restrain a man by his private will, he cannot act freely in what the state's code does not permit, and if he could, this would be harming a man's rights by one man's force. It destroys the public way of the law and starts a great evil in the human world, and who would call it acceptable? A person's body ought to be treated with the respect of uprightness and the leniency of fairness. Hence, even if one suppresses a man's will, places him in a vast hall, feeds him rich meat and fine grain and clothes him in brocade, this is confinement; and to forcibly halt a man's walking on the road is no different from confinement. The right of the person lies solely in leaving a man free so long as he has not broken the state's laws, and in defending him against injury from outside.

paragraphs.orig: 財産의權利ᄅᆞᆯ顧ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ亦人生의一大緊重ᄒᆞᆫ事니各人이各其自己의所有ᄒᆞᆫ財産을保守ᄒᆞ야一芥라도人을不與ᄒᆞ든지千金으로其心志의樂을窮ᄒᆞ든지國家의法律을不背ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ禁抑ᄒᆞ기不可ᄒᆞ고又或暴徒의侵奪이有ᄒᆞᆫ則法律의公道ᄅᆞᆯ依賴ᄒᆞ야其護守ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ力을受홈이可ᄒᆞ니蓋人의私有ᄒᆞᆫ物을國法으로保守케홈은至大ᄒᆞᆫ惠擇이라妨害ᄅᆞᆯ不加ᄒᆞ기에不止ᄒᆞ고極臻히保護ᄒᆞ야秋毫도侵犯홈이有ᄒᆞ면不可ᄒᆞ니全國人民의普同ᄒᆞᆫ大利ᄅᆞᆯ興作ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ事件이有ᄒᆞ야도一人의私有ᄅᆞᆯ害ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ行ᄒᆞ기不敢ᄒᆞᆫ者라假令此에一條新路ᄅᆞᆯ開ᄒᆞ기에一民의私有ᄒᆞᆫ地面을交亘ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ此擧가雖公衆을爲ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大便利나然ᄒᆞ나主人의準諾을不得ᄒᆞᆫ則其地ᄅᆞᆯ犯ᄒᆞ기不敢ᄒᆞ니如此ᄒᆞᆫ時ᄅᆞᆯ當ᄒᆞ야ᄂᆞᆫ國法으로處寘ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞ야其人으로ᄒᆞ야곰至當ᄒᆞᆫ價値에放賣ᄒᆞ기ᄅᆞᆯ令호ᄃᆡ決斷코威力을恣홈이無ᄒᆞ고謹愼을加ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니今此引喩ᄂᆞᆫ其一例ᄅᆞᆯ擧示홈이라千事萬物이各人의私有에屬ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ國法의保護가至愼至密ᄒᆞ야不貴不重ᄒᆞᆫ者가無ᄒᆞ니千金子의狐貉과乞人의一弊衣가物品의高下ᄂᆞᆫ懸殊ᄒᆞ나各一人의私有되기ᄂᆞᆫ同ᄒᆞᆫ則國法의保護ᄂᆞᆫ差等을不立홈이라然ᄒᆞᆫ故로財産의權利ᄂᆞᆫ國家의法律에不戾ᄒᆞᆫ則萬乘의威라도是ᄅᆞᆯ奪ᄒᆞ기不能ᄒᆞ며萬人의敵이라도是ᄅᆞᆯ動ᄒᆞ기不敢ᄒᆞ야其與奪이法에在ᄒᆞ고人에不在ᄒᆞ니此ᄂᆞᆫ公權으로私物을保守ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大道라
paragraphs.modern: 財産의 權利를 顧하건대 亦人生의 一大緊重한 事니 各人이 各其自己의 所有한 財産을 保守하여 一芥라도 人을 不與하든지 千金으로 其心志의 樂을 窮하든지 國家의 法律을 不背하는 時는 禁抑하기 不可하고 又或暴徒의 侵奪이 有한 則法律의 公道를 依賴하여 其護守하는 力을 受함이 可하니 蓋人의 私有한 物을 國法으로 保守케 함은 至大한 惠擇이라 妨害를 不加하기에 不止하고 極臻히 保護하여 秋毫도 侵犯함이 有하면 不可하니 全國人民의 普同한 大利를 興作하는 事件이 有하여도 一人의 私有를 害할진대 行하기 不敢한 者라 假令此에 一條新路를 開하기에 一民의 私有한 地面을 交亘하는 時는 此擧가 雖公衆을 爲하는 大便利나 然하나 主人의 準諾을 不得한 則其地를 犯하기 不敢하니 如此한 時를 當하여는 國法으로 處寘하는 道를 行하여 其人으로 하여금 至當한 價値에 放賣하기를 令하되 決斷코 威力을 恣함이 無하고 謹愼을 加하나니 今此引喩는 其一例를 擧示함이라 千事萬物이 各人의 私有에 屬한 者는 國法의 保護가 至愼至密하여 不貴不重한 者가 無하니 千金子의 狐貉과 乞人의 一弊衣가 物品의 高下는 懸殊하나 各一人의 私有되기는 同한 則國法의 保護는 差等을 不立함이라 然한 故로 財産의 權利는 國家의 法律에 不戾한 則萬乘의 威라도 是를 奪하기 不能하며 萬人의 敵이라도 是를 動하기 不敢하여 其與奪이 法에 在하고 人에 不在하니 此는 公權으로 私物을 保守하는 大道라
paragraphs.en: Turning to the right of property: this too is a weighty matter of human life. So long as each person guards his own possessions, whether he gives not even a mustard seed to anyone or uses a thousand pieces of gold to the full measure of his heart's pleasure, provided he does not violate the laws of the state, he may not be forbidden or suppressed; and if violent men plunder him, he may rely on the public way of the law and receive its power of protection. That the law of the state should safeguard what a person privately holds is a most weighty benefit. It is not enough merely not to interfere; it must protect him to the utmost, and it is not right that even the slightest infringement occur. Even if there is some undertaking that would bring great benefit to all the people of the nation, if it would harm the private property of one person, no one dares to carry it out. For example, in opening a new road, if it crosses a piece of land privately owned by one of the people, although this enterprise would be of great convenience to the public, if the owner's permission is not obtained no one dares to trespass on that land. In such a case, one follows the way of disposition by the law of the state, ordering the man to sell at a fully proper price, and in no way does one indulge force but adds caution. This illustration is only a single example. Among all things privately owned by individuals, the state's protection is most careful and close, and nothing is of too little worth to be protected: the fox and badger furs of a man of a thousand gold pieces and a beggar's single ragged garment differ greatly in the grade of the goods, but since each is equally one man's private property, the state's protection draws no difference of rank. Therefore the right of property, so long as it does not run against the state's laws, cannot be taken even by the might of a ten-thousand-chariot ruler, and cannot be moved even by an enemy of ten thousand men; giving and taking lies with the law and not with persons. This is the great way of guarding private goods by public authority.

paragraphs.orig: 營業의權利ᄅᆞᆯ議ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ人이世에生ᄒᆞᆷ에其生活ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道가此ᄅᆞᆯ因ᄒᆞ야立ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로亦人生의不可無ᄒᆞᆫ要務니國法에不違ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ各其才의能ᄒᆞᆫᄃᆡ로其心의樂ᄒᆞᆫ바ᄅᆞᆯ營逐ᄒᆞ야他人의抑遏과妨碍ᄅᆞᆯ不受ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ지라士農工商의業에貴賤의區分을不立ᄒᆞ며爾我의事功을各治ᄒᆞ야心勞와力役의獲致ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ利益을享受ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니大槪新書의著述과新物의發造가人世의裨益을可助ᄒᆞᆯ者ᄂᆞᆫ其本主에게專賣權을許施ᄒᆞ야年限을酌定ᄒᆞ고國法으로護守ᄒᆞ야他人의侵犯ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ弊ᄅᆞᆯ抑止ᄒᆞ기ᄂᆞᆫ亦特異ᄒᆞᆫ權利ᄅᆞᆯ附與ᄒᆞ야其莫大ᄒᆞᆫ勤勞ᄅᆞᆯ償ᄒᆞ고因ᄒᆞ야世人의智巧ᄅᆞᆯ鼓勵홈이어니와如何ᄒᆞᆫ事業이든지大小ᄅᆞᆯ勿論ᄒᆞ고倡開ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者가必先政府의許準을獲ᄒᆞᆫ然後에其營求ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ事工을任從홈이可ᄒᆞ고又政府도其營求ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ工業의趣意ᄅᆞᆯ試考ᄒᆞ야國家의法律을遵合ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ不許홈이亦無ᄒᆞ니然ᄒᆞᆫ故로營業의權利ᄂᆞᆫ國法의禁止ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ條例ᄅᆞᆯ不犯ᄒᆞ면拘碍ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ端緖가自無홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 營業의 權利를 議하건대 人이 世에 生함에 其生活하는 道가 此를 因하여 立하는 故로 亦人生의 不可無한 要務니 國法에 不違하는 時는 各其才의 能한 대로 其心의 樂한 바를 營逐하여 他人의 抑遏과 妨碍를 不受하는지라 士農工商의 業에 貴賤의 區分을 不立하며 爾我의 事功을 各治하여 心勞와 力役의 獲致하는 利益을 享受하나니 大槪新書의 著述과 新物의 發造가 人世의 裨益을 可助할 者는 其本主에게 專賣權을 許施하여 年限을 酌定하고 國法으로 護守하여 他人의 侵犯하는 弊를 抑止하기는 亦特異한 權利를 附與하여 其莫大한 勤勞를 償하고 因하여 世人의 智巧를 鼓勵함이어니와 如何한 事業이든지 大小를 勿論하고 倡開하는 者가 必先政府의 許準을 獲한 然後에 其營求하는 事工을 任從함이 可하고 又政府도 其營求하는 工業의 趣意를 試考하여 國家의 法律을 遵合한 者는 不許함이 亦無하니 然한 故로 營業의 權利는 國法의 禁止하는 條例를 不犯하면 拘碍하는 端緖가 自無함이라
paragraphs.en: Discussing the right of occupation: since a person's way of making a living is set up by this, it is an indispensable duty of human life. So long as one does not offend the state's laws, each pursues what his heart enjoys according to his ability, without suppression or hindrance from others; among the occupations of scholar, farmer, artisan and merchant no distinction of noble and humble is set up, each attends to his own work, and each enjoys the profit gained by labour of mind and exertion of strength. In general, for the writing of new books and the making of new things that can benefit the human world, the exclusive right of sale is granted to the original owner, a term of years is fixed, and the law guards it and stops others from infringing; this grants a special additional right, compensates his enormous toil, and in turn encourages the ingenuity of the world. But whatever the enterprise, large or small, it is proper that the one who initiates it first obtain the government's permission and then carry on his work; and the government too, examining the purport of the work he seeks to undertake, does not refuse one that conforms to the laws of the state. Therefore the right of occupation is such that, so long as one does not violate the clauses the state's law forbids, no thread of obstruction arises of itself.

paragraphs.orig: 集會의權利ᄅᆞᆯ究ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ人生의相與ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大道라和平ᄒᆞᆫ意思로友好ᄒᆞᆫ情誼ᄅᆞᆯ表ᄒᆞ기爲홈이든지重大ᄒᆞᆫ事工으로廣博ᄒᆞᆫ議論을採ᄒᆞ기爲홈이든지國法을遵守ᄒᆞ야禁例에無違ᄒᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ制止홈이不可ᄒᆞ니大槪暇日의風致ᄅᆞᆯ消遣ᄒᆞ야朋侶의宴會ᄂᆞᆫ人生의志氣ᄅᆞᆯ舒暢ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ樂事며深妙ᄒᆞᆫ物理ᄅᆞᆯ窮格ᄒᆞ야演說의約集은人生의知識을開導ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ好機며巨大ᄒᆞᆫ功役을經營ᄒᆞ야衆人의會議ᄂᆞᆫ世間의便利ᄅᆞᆯ增益ᄒᆞ고高明ᄒᆞᆫ學科ᄅᆞᆯ問難ᄒᆞ야諸士의集萃ᄂᆞᆫ天下의風敎ᄅᆞᆯ振起ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니大槪人이衆을成ᄒᆞᆫ則大功을起ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ지라國中의人民이交際ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道ᄅᆞᆯ善修ᄒᆞ야聲氣의相同으로求應ᄒᆞ고各其樂赴ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ能事로會ᄅᆞᆯ立ᄒᆞ며社ᄅᆞᆯ結ᄒᆞ야大者ᄂᆞᆫ公衆에普洽ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ功業을企圖ᄒᆞ고小者ᄂᆞᆫ一社一會의偏利小事ᄅᆞᆯ營求호ᄃᆡ其自立ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ規制와相守ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ約條ᄂᆞᆫ他人의侵侮ᄒᆞ기ᄅᆞᆯ不願ᄒᆞ고又或他人의事故ᄅᆞᆯ因ᄒᆞ야有時其成就ᄅᆞᆯ稽緩ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ弊가不無ᄒᆞᆫ則亦國法의保護ᄅᆞᆯ不行ᄒᆞ면不可ᄒᆞ거니와偏黨의過激ᄒᆞᆫ集議와僻地의秘密ᄒᆞᆫ約會며又恒産을不執ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ徒輩의喧噪聚合은皆國法의攸禁이라然ᄒᆞᆫ故로集會의權利ᄂᆞᆫ國禁을不踰ᄒᆞᆫ則其意ᄅᆞᆯ任從ᄒᆞ야些少의牽掣이不至홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 集會의 權利를 究하건대 人生의 相與하는 大道라 和平한 意思로 友好한 情誼를 表하기 爲함이든지 重大한 事工으로 廣博한 議論을 採하기 爲함이든지 國法을 遵守하여 禁例에 無違한 時는 制止함이 不可하니 大槪暇日의 風致를 消遣하여 朋侶의 宴會는 人生의 志氣를 舒暢하는 樂事며 深妙한 物理를 窮格하여 演說의 約集은 人生의 知識을 開導하는 好機며 巨大한 功役을 經營하여 衆人의 會議는 世間의 便利를 增益하고 高明한 學科를 問難하여 諸士의 集萃는 天下의 風敎를 振起하나니 大槪人이 衆을 成한 則大功을 起하는지라 國中의 人民이 交際하는 道를 善修하여 聲氣의 相同으로 求應하고 各其樂赴하는 能事로 會를 立하며 社를 結하여 大者는 公衆에 普洽하는 功業을 企圖하고 小者는 一社一會의 偏利小事를 營求하되 其自立하는 規制와 相守하는 約條는 他人의 侵侮하기를 不願하고 又或他人의 事故를 因하여 有時其成就를 稽緩하는 弊가 不無한 則亦國法의 保護를 不行하면 不可하거니와 偏黨의 過激한 集議와 僻地의 秘密한 約會며 又恒産을 不執하는 徒輩의 喧噪聚合은 皆國法의 攸禁이라 然한 故로 集會의 權利는 國禁을 不踰한 則其意를 任從하여 些少의 牽掣이 不至함이라
paragraphs.en: Examining the right of assembly: it is the great way of mutual intercourse in human life. Whether it is to express friendly affection with a peaceful intention, or to gather broad discussion for a weighty undertaking, so long as one obeys the state's laws and does not offend prohibitions, it must not be stopped. A friends' banquet to pass the leisure of a free day is a pleasure that relaxes the spirit of life; a lecture gathering that probes the profound principles of things is a good occasion to open up human knowledge; a meeting of many people to plan some great work adds to the convenience of the world; a gathering of scholars to question and debate lofty branches of learning rouses the culture of the whole world. When people form a multitude they achieve great things. When the people of a country cultivate well the way of fellowship, respond to one another as voices of one spirit, and each founds an association or forms a society around the work he gladly takes up, the greater ones plan enterprises that benefit the public at large and the lesser ones seek the partial gains and small affairs of one society or one group; but the regulations they establish for themselves and the agreements they keep are not to be insulted by others, and where at times their accomplishment is delayed through the troubles of others, the protection of the state's law must be applied. However, extremist partisan assemblies, secret meetings in remote places, and the noisy gatherings of persons with no fixed livelihood are all forbidden by the state's law. Therefore the right of assembly is such that, so long as one does not overstep the state's prohibitions, one follows one's own will, and not the slightest restraint reaches it.

paragraphs.orig: 宗敎의權利ᄅᆞᆯ擧ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ亦人生의一大關係니夫宗敎ᄂᆞᆫ世人의心行을管制ᄒᆞ며浸感ᄒᆞ야人建ᄒᆞᆫ大道라天下의至廣홈으로世俗의宗尙ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ敎가一에不歸ᄒᆞ고各其門戶ᄅᆞᆯ立ᄒᆞ야宗敎의殊異ᄅᆞᆯ生ᄒᆞ니人世의不幸이此에莫大ᄒᆞ나然ᄒᆞ나此亦大衆의信服ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者며彼亦大衆의崇奉ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者로大衆의綱紀ᄅᆞᆯ維持ᄒᆞ기ᄂᆞᆫ其道가同ᄒᆞᆫ則人을勸ᄒᆞ야邪ᄅᆞᆯ棄ᄒᆞ고正에歸ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大旨ᄂᆞᆫ亦相近ᄒᆞᆫ基礎에成立홈이라不然이면奈何로大衆의悅服ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者되야千百載의久遠을相傳ᄒᆞ리오是故로各人이各其心의悅樂ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ宗敎에信依ᄒᆞ야國法을敬奉ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ其心의所好ᄅᆞᆯ强奪홈과其身의所歸ᄅᆞᆯ勒禁홈이不可ᄒᆞ니泰西人의今古歷史ᄅᆞᆯ考ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ宗敎의爭論으로人心을搖動ᄒᆞ며人國을滅亡ᄒᆞ야殺伐의大害가不尠ᄒᆞᆫ지라羅馬의舊代에天主敎의新播홈으로前後數十萬人命을坑殺ᄒᆞ며伊太利佛蘭西等國의近古에新舊敎의紛爭으로亦數十萬人의生命을殺戮ᄒᆞ야人民의移散이不少ᄒᆞ고英吉利ᄂᆞᆫ新敎의宗旨ᄅᆞᆯ專尙ᄒᆞ야國內他宗의敎ᄅᆞᆯ嚴禁ᄒᆞ나阿爾蘭島民은元來天主敎ᄅᆞᆯ信服ᄒᆞ야政府의命을不從홈으로又其法을改ᄒᆞ야宗敎ᄂᆞᆫ各人의意에任호ᄃᆡ又一法을建ᄒᆞ야國家의任政ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大臣은新敎宗門의人야니면才德이具備ᄒᆞᆫ者라도擢用을不許ᄒᆞ니是ᄅᆞᆯ由ᄒᆞ야天主敎에歸依ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ家ᄅᆞᆯ擧ᄒᆞ야外國에徙居홈이極多홈이라若玆ᄒᆞᆫ事由로推比ᄒᆞ야熟揣ᄒᆞᆫ則宗敎의彼此ᄅᆞᆯ分ᄒᆞ야一許一禁이國家의政治에小利도不生ᄒᆞ고大害ᄅᆞᆯ反成ᄒᆞ야其實이此宗을爲ᄒᆞ야彼宗을排斥ᄒᆞ기에不過홈이니政府의力을假借ᄒᆞ야他宗을排斥ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ自然其心이洽滿ᄒᆞ거니와其排斥을被ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ其心이不平ᄒᆞ야其身이雖其國에居ᄒᆞ야도其政府ᄅᆞᆯ敵視ᄒᆞ고服信ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ宗門에願忠ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ性氣가益固ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니此ᄂᆞᆫ天下各邦의已然ᄒᆞᆫ景像이오古今의同然ᄒᆞᆫ弊害라政治의一視ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ公心은各人의崇信ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ宗敎의異同을不問ᄒᆞ고其權利의保護ᄂᆞᆫ無偏ᄒᆞ야其人을人ᄒᆞᆯᄯᆞᄅᆞᆷ이오惟其敎典의條例가人生의倫綱을壞ᄒᆞ야國法에背ᄒᆞᆫ則禁止ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니然ᄒᆞᆫ故로宗敎의權利ᄂᆞᆫ國家의典常을不犯ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ其歸依ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ信心을各從홈이라
paragraphs.modern: 宗敎의 權利를 擧하건대 亦人生의 一大關係니 夫宗敎는 世人의 心行을 管制하며 浸感하여 人建한 大道라 天下의 至廣함으로 世俗의 宗尙하는 敎가 一에 不歸하고 各其門戶를 立하여 宗敎의 殊異를 生하니 人世의 不幸이 此에 莫大하나 然하나 此亦大衆의 信服하는 者며 彼亦大衆의 崇奉하는 者로 大衆의 綱紀를 維持하기는 其道가 同한 則人을 勸하여 邪를 棄하고 正에 歸하는 大旨는 亦相近한 基礎에 成立함이라 不然이면 奈何로 大衆의 悅服하는 者되어 千百載의 久遠을 相傳하리오 是故로 各人이 各其心의 悅樂하는 宗敎에 信依하여 國法을 敬奉하는 時는 其心의 所好를 强奪함과 其身의 所歸를 勒禁함이 不可하니 泰西人의 今古歷史를 考하건대 宗敎의 爭論으로 人心을 搖動하며 人國을 滅亡하여 殺伐의 大害가 不尠한지라 羅馬의 舊代에 天主敎의 新播함으로 前後數十萬人命을 坑殺하며 伊太利佛蘭西等國의 近古에 新舊敎의 紛爭으로 亦數十萬人의 生命을 殺戮하여 人民의 移散이 不少하고 英吉利는 新敎의 宗旨를 專尙하여 國內他宗의 敎를 嚴禁하나 阿爾蘭島民은 元來天主敎를 信服하여 政府의 命을 不從함으로 又其法을 改하여 宗敎는 各人의 意에 任하되 又一法을 建하여 國家의 任政하는 大臣은 新敎宗門의 人 아니면 才德이 具備한 者라도 擢用을 不許하니 是를 由하여 天主敎에 歸依한 者는 家를 擧하여 外國에 徙居함이 極多함이라 若玆한 事由로 推比하여 熟揣한 則宗敎의 彼此를 分하여 一許一禁이 國家의 政治에 小利도 不生하고 大害를 反成하여 其實이 此宗을 爲하여 彼宗을 排斥하기에 不過함이니 政府의 力을 假借하여 他宗을 排斥하는 者는 自然其心이 洽滿하거니와 其排斥을 被하는 者는 其心이 不平하여 其身이 雖其國에 居하여도 其政府를 敵視하고 服信하는 宗門에 願忠하는 性氣가 益固하나니 此는 天下各邦의 已然한 景像이오 古今의 同然한 弊害라 政治의 一視하는 公心은 各人의 崇信하는 宗敎의 異同을 不問하고 其權利의 保護는 無偏하여 其人을 人할 따름이오 惟其敎典의 條例가 人生의 倫綱을 壞하여 國法에 背한 則禁止하나니 然한 故로 宗敎의 權利는 國家의 典常을 不犯하는 時는 其歸依하는 信心을 各從함이라
paragraphs.en: Taking up the right of religion: this too is a matter of great importance in human life. Religion is the great way built by men that governs and gradually permeates the minds and conduct of people. Because the world is vast, the teachings that people revere do not return to one but each sets up its own house, and differences of religion arise; there is no greater misfortune in the human world than this. Yet this one too is believed by the multitude, and that one too is revered by the multitude; for upholding the order of the multitude, since their way is the same, the main purpose of urging people to cast off evil and return to what is right is founded on a similar basis. Otherwise, how could they have become what the multitude gladly submit to and been handed down for a thousand years? Therefore, when each person trusts the religion his own heart delights in and respectfully obeys the laws of the state, it is not right to seize by force what his heart prefers or to forbid by compulsion where his person turns. Looking at the histories of Western peoples, past and present, religious disputes have stirred people's hearts and destroyed nations, and the great harms of slaughter have not been few: in ancient Rome, with the new spread of the Catholic faith, several hundred thousand people were buried alive, before and after; in recent times in Italy, France and other countries, strife between old and new faith likewise killed hundreds of thousands and scattered no small number of people; England has devoted itself to the doctrine of the new faith and strictly forbidden the teachings of other sects within the country, but the people of the Irish island, who from the first believed in Catholicism, did not obey the government's order, so England changed its law again, leaving religion to each person's will, yet established another law that ministers conducting the state's government must be of the new faith and that even a man fully endowed with talent and virtue, if not, would not be permitted to be promoted; for this reason those who had returned to Catholicism, taking their whole households, moved abroad in very large numbers. Weighing such circumstances carefully, to divide religions into this and that, permitting one and forbidding another, brings not the slightest benefit to a state's government but instead works great harm; in fact it comes to no more than excluding that sect for the sake of this one. Those who borrow the power of the government to exclude other sects are naturally satisfied in heart, but those who suffer the exclusion are discontented in heart, and though they live in that country they regard the government as an enemy, and their disposition to be loyal to the sect they trust grows ever firmer. This is the condition already seen in the countries of the world, and a harm shared by past and present. The impartial mind of government, regardless of the differences among the religions people revere, protects their rights without bias and simply treats those people as people; only where the regulations of a religious code destroy the human bonds of life and run against the law of the state does it forbid. Therefore the right of religion is such that, so long as one does not offend the norms of the state, each follows the faith in which he places his trust.

paragraphs.orig: 言詞의自由ᄅᆞᆯ釋ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ人生權利의一條라大抵人의思量이聲音으로發ᄒᆞ면言詞며形像으로記ᄒᆞ면文字니然ᄒᆞᆫ故로二者ᄅᆞᆯ合ᄒᆞ야言詞의權利에俱歸홈이라不根ᄒᆞᆫ是非로無禮ᄒᆞᆫ毁謗을他人에加홈과且私心의好惡로政治의得失을妄論홈은國禁의所在어니와事狀의實境을據ᄒᆞ야眞確ᄒᆞᆫ議評을立ᄒᆞ기ᄂᆞᆫ各人이其意ᄅᆞᆯ任ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니寃抑이是ᄅᆞᆯ藉ᄒᆞ야伸ᄒᆞ며禍害가是ᄅᆞᆯ山ᄒᆞ야祛ᄒᆞ며善良이是ᄅᆞᆯ賴ᄒᆞ야闡ᄒᆞ고又人世의千事萬物에至ᄒᆞ야도是가無ᄒᆞ면其功用의著發이必難ᄒᆞᆫ지라世의治亂과人의賢否ᄅᆞᆯ隨ᄒᆞ야此權利의多少ᄅᆞᆯ判定ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로亂世의苛法은偶語ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄅᆞᆯ市에棄ᄒᆞ고聖人의美規ᄂᆞᆫ誹謗의木을立ᄒᆞ야天下의善言을來홈이니惟口ᄂᆞᆫ好ᄅᆞᆯ出ᄒᆞ며戎을興ᄒᆞ야禍福의樞機ᄅᆞᆯ是作ᄒᆞᆫ則君子의謹愼ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ道에縬守ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ箴戒가可ᄒᆞ다謂ᄒᆞ나然ᄒᆞ나人이世에居ᄒᆞᆷ에必其思慮가有ᄒᆞ고且其思慮ᄂᆞᆫ事物에觸ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫᄃᆡ로發ᄒᆞ야喜哀和激이其常이無ᄒᆞ니法律이雖密ᄒᆞ야도萬姓의口ᄅᆞᆯ箝ᄒᆞ야一大群의有舌ᄒᆞᆫ啞子ᄅᆞᆯ化成ᄒᆞ기ᄂᆞᆫ不能홈이라是以로人民의言路ᄅᆞᆯ廣開ᄒᆞ야鄙陋ᄒᆞᆫ俗尙과貪汚ᄒᆞᆫ習氣와詐僞ᄒᆞᆫ行實이며不公不平ᄒᆞᆫ施措ᄅᆞᆯ演說의宏辨으로論駁ᄒᆞ며新聞의廣詢으로指擧ᄒᆞ야民人의行動이此ᄅᆞᆯ顧忌ᄒᆞ며官吏의縱橫이此ᄅᆞᆯ畏憚ᄒᆞᆫ則亦世道의維持ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ一大助로ᄃᆡ萬若浮虛不實ᄒᆞᆫ者가有ᄒᆞ면法律의公道로是ᄅᆞᆯ懲勵홈이亦可ᄒᆞ니然ᄒᆞ기言詞의權利ᄂᆞᆫ人人이皆有ᄒᆞ야正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로國禁을不違ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ時ᄂᆞᆫ他人의操縱을不受ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라
paragraphs.modern: 言詞의 自由를 釋하건대 人生權利의 一條라 大抵人의 思量이 聲音으로 發하면 言詞며 形像으로 記하면 文字니 然한 故로 二者를 合하여 言詞의 權利에 俱歸함이라 不根한 是非로 無禮한 毁謗을 他人에 加함과 且私心의 好惡로 政治의 得失을 妄論함은 國禁의 所在어니와 事狀의 實境을 據하여 眞確한 議評을 立하기는 各人이 其意를 任하나니 寃抑이 是를 藉하여 伸하며 禍害가 是를 山하여 祛하며 善良이 是를 賴하여 闡하고 又人世의 千事萬物에 至하여도 是가 無하면 其功用의 著發이 必難한지라 世의 治亂과 人의 賢否를 隨하여 此權利의 多少를 判定하는 故로 亂世의 苛法은 偶語하는 者를 市에 棄하고 聖人의 美規는 誹謗의 木을 立하여 天下의 善言을 來함이니 惟口는 好를 出하며 戎을 興하여 禍福의 樞機를 是作한 則君子의 謹愼하는 道에 縬守하는 箴戒가 可하다 謂하나 然하나 人이 世에 居함에 必其思慮가 有하고 且其思慮는 事物에 觸하는 대로 發하여 喜哀和激이 其常이 無하니 法律이 雖密하여도 萬姓의 口를 箝하여 一大群의 有舌한 啞子를 化成하기는 不能함이라 是以로 人民의 言路를 廣開하여 鄙陋한 俗尙과 貪汚한 習氣와 詐僞한 行實이며 不公不平한 施措를 演說의 宏辨으로 論駁하며 新聞의 廣詢으로 指擧하여 民人의 行動이 此를 顧忌하며 官吏의 縱橫이 此를 畏憚한 則亦世道의 維持하는 一大助로되 萬若浮虛不實한 者가 有하면 法律의 公道로 是를 懲勵함이 亦可하니 然하기 言詞의 權利는 人人이 皆有하여 正直한 道로 國禁을 不違하는 時는 他人의 操縱을 不受하는 者라
paragraphs.en: Explaining liberty of speech: it is one article of the rights of human life. In general, when a person's thought is uttered in sound it is speech, and when it is recorded in visible form it is writing; so the two together belong to the right of speech. To heap groundless right-and-wrong and discourteous slander on others, and to recklessly discuss the gains and losses of government according to private likes and dislikes, are matters the state forbids; but to make a true and accurate critique on the basis of the real circumstances of events is left to each person's will. By this, grievances are redressed, calamities are dispelled and the good and virtuous are brought to light; and in all the affairs and things of the human world, without this their useful effects would be hard to display. Following the order or disorder of an age and the worth or worthlessness of men, the amount of this right is determined; therefore the harsh law of a disordered age casts out in the marketplace (i.e. executes) those who merely speak together, while the fine rule of the sage sets up the 'wood of slander' to bring in the good words of all under heaven. 'The mouth gives forth good and raises armies,' and it is the pivot of fortune and misfortune; so it may be said that the gentleman's way of caution does well to keep to its admonitions. Yet when a person lives in the world he necessarily has thoughts, and those thoughts are uttered according to what he comes across, with no constancy of joy, sorrow, harmony or anger; even a strict law cannot gag the mouths of ten thousand families and turn a great crowd of tongued people into mutes. So if the road of the people's speech is opened wide and vulgar customs, corrupt habits, deceitful conduct and unfair, unjust measures are refuted by the eloquence of lectures and exposed by the broad inquiries of newspapers, so that the people's actions are mindful of this and officials' high-handedness is afraid of it, this too is a great help in sustaining the way of the world; and if there is some baseless falsehood, it is also right to punish it by the public way of the law. Thus the right of speech is held by every person, and so long as he does not violate the state's prohibitions by the upright way, he is subject to no one's control.

paragraphs.orig: 名譽의通義ᄅᆞᆯ解ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ亦人生의一大權利라其實은身命의權利에歸屬ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者니夫名譽ᄂᆞᆫ人의等品을隨ᄒᆞ야其才藝及性質의實像을斷定ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ聲價인則世間에需售ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ方道가是ᄅᆞᆯ依ᄒᆞ야立ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ지라此通義가他人의虧傷을一被ᄒᆞᆫ則一身의面目을頓失ᄒᆞ야各般權利의遏止홈이身命의不自由와同ᄒᆞᆫ故로他人의名譽ᄅᆞᆯ損傷홈이其肢體ᄅᆞᆯ毁疵홈과無異ᄒᆞ니是以로爽實ᄒᆞᆫ事端을提ᄒᆞ야無禮ᄒᆞᆫ誹謗을起ᄒᆞ며疑似ᄒᆞᆫ傳聞을因ᄒᆞ야不敬ᄒᆞᆫ毁斥을行ᄒᆞ며嫌惡ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ私故ᄅᆞᆯ由ᄒᆞ야暖昧ᄒᆞᆫ罪辜ᄅᆞᆯ構ᄒᆞ며偏黨의氣習을縱ᄒᆞ야吹覓ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ讒譏ᄅᆞᆯ恣ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ諸事로人의聲聞을汙穢ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ國法의不許홈인故로毁名律의條例ᄅᆞᆯ設ᄒᆞ야如此ᄒᆞᆫ惡行을禁斷ᄒᆞ야人의寃屈을伸直ᄒᆞ고名譽ᄅᆞᆯ保護홈이니然ᄒᆞ기公衆의交際ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ大道ᄅᆞᆯ保ᄒᆞ야是非와長短의妄議가不行ᄒᆞ고欺蔽와詐僞의鄙習이自消ᄒᆞ야廉恥의節操로其躬을飭ᄒᆞ며禮義의品行으로其心을勵ᄒᆞ고相敬ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ主義ᄅᆞᆯ務ᄒᆞ야凡事에誠實ᄒᆞ기로爲要호ᄃᆡ如何ᄒᆞᆫ人의如何ᄒᆞᆫ事든지其現實이分明ᄒᆞ야世道와人心에有關ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ演說或新聞으로天下에公布ᄒᆞ야도其人이伸辨ᄒᆞ기亦不能ᄒᆞ니然ᄒᆞᆫ故로名譽의權利ᄂᆞᆫ正直ᄒᆞᆫ道로自守ᄒᆞ고國家의法律을敬遵ᄒᆞᆫ則他人의毁汚ᄅᆞᆯ不被ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라
paragraphs.modern: 名譽의 通義를 解하건대 亦人生의 一大權利라 其實은 身命의 權利에 歸屬하는 者니 夫名譽는 人의 等品을 隨하여 其才藝及性質의 實像을 斷定하는 聲價인 則世間에 需售하는 方道가 是를 依하여 立하는지라 此通義가 他人의 虧傷을 一被한 則一身의 面目을 頓失하여 各般權利의 遏止함이 身命의 不自由와 同한 故로 他人의 名譽를 損傷함이 其肢體를 毁疵함과 無異하니 是以로 爽實한 事端을 提하여 無禮한 誹謗을 起하며 疑似한 傳聞을 因하여 不敬한 毁斥을 行하며 嫌惡하는 私故를 由하여 暖昧한 罪辜를 構하며 偏黨의 氣習을 縱하여 吹覓하는 讒譏를 恣하는 諸事로 人의 聲聞을 汙穢하는 者는 國法의 不許함인 故로 毁名律의 條例를 設하여 如此한 惡行을 禁斷하여 人의 寃屈을 伸直하고 名譽를 保護함이니 然하기 公衆의 交際하는 大道를 保하여 是非와 長短의 妄議가 不行하고 欺蔽와 詐僞의 鄙習이 自消하여 廉恥의 節操로 其躬을 飭하며 禮義의 品行으로 其心을 勵하고 相敬하는 主義를 務하여 凡事에 誠實하기로 爲要하되 如何한 人의 如何한 事든지 其現實이 分明하여 世道와 人心에 有關한 者는 演說或新聞으로 天下에 公布하여도 其人이 伸辨하기 亦不能하니 然한 故로 名譽의 權利는 正直한 道로 自守하고 國家의 法律을 敬遵한 則他人의 毁汚를 不被하는 者라
paragraphs.en: Explaining the rightful claim of reputation: this too is a great right of human life; in fact it belongs to the right of the person. Reputation is the standing that determines the true image of a person's talent and character according to his rank, and the means by which one is valued in the world are established on it. When this rightful claim suffers injury from another, one's face is lost at once and the stopping of various rights is the same as the unfreedom of the person; therefore damaging another's reputation is no different from maiming his limbs. Accordingly, those who raise baseless pretexts to start discourteous slander, make disrespectful denunciations on the strength of doubtful hearsay, concoct vague accusations from hated private grudges, or give free rein to partisan habits and indulge in hunted-up slanders, all such things that defile a person's reputation are not permitted by the state's law; so clauses of a defamation law are established to put a stop to such evil acts, to redress people's wrongs and to protect their reputation. In this way the great way of public intercourse is preserved, groundless talk of right and wrong and faults and merits is not practised, the vulgar habits of deceit and fraud vanish of themselves, one regulates one's person with the integrity of a sense of shame, spurs one's heart with conduct of propriety and righteousness, strives for the principle of mutual respect and makes sincerity in all things the essential; yet whatever man and whatever matter, if the reality is clear and bears on the way of the world and the hearts of men, and it is published to the world by lecture or newspaper, that man likewise cannot defend himself against it. Therefore the right of reputation is such that, if one guards oneself by the upright way and respectfully obeys the state's laws, one suffers no defilement from others.

paragraphs.orig: 此로由ᄒᆞ야觀ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ人生의諸般權利가雖其天生의備具ᄒᆞᆫ者나人爲ᄒᆞᆫ法律의關係로其分度의增減이有ᄒᆞᆫ지라天授ᄒᆞᆫ權利ᄅᆞᆯ人力으로操縱ᄒᆞ기不可ᄒᆞ다ᄒᆞ야其自便을任寘ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ放蕩ᄒᆞᆫ弊俗과壤亂ᄒᆞᆫ惡習이日로增ᄒᆞ며月로加ᄒᆞ야其涯涘의浩大홈이測度ᄒᆞ기不能ᄒᆞ리니四端과五倫의綱紀와秩序ᄅᆞᆯ依憑ᄒᆞ야法律의禁防이極密ᄒᆞᆫ制ᄅᆞᆯ設ᄒᆞ며至愼ᄒᆞᆫ規ᄅᆞᆯ立ᄒᆞ야도猶且其千岐萬條의絲棼毫細ᄒᆞᆫ橫恣性과放縱心은鋤除ᄒᆞ기不盡ᄒᆞ며剪滅ᄒᆞ기甚難ᄒᆞ야娼妓의淫을賣홈은自己가自己의心으로禽獸의自由ᄅᆞᆯ行홈이오奴婢의世로傳홈은他人이他人의身에蠻夷의通義ᄅᆞᆯ存홈이로ᄃᆡ習俗의浸潤으로人世의常事ᄅᆞᆯ狃成ᄒᆞ야法律의公正ᄒᆞᆫ道理와威力으로도抑遏ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ功을難期ᄒᆞ니如此ᄒᆞᆫ弊風惡俗도各其人의權利라謂홈이可ᄒᆞᆯ가否라凡事ᄅᆞᆯ行ᄒᆞ야其心에可ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ天下人이皆曰可라ᄒᆞᆯ디며行ᄒᆞ야其心에不可ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ天下人이亦皆曰不可라ᄒᆞᆯ디니大抵人의自由와通義ᄂᆞᆫ天下人의普同ᄒᆞᆫ權利라然ᄒᆞᆫ故로一人의可不可가天下人의同然ᄒᆞᆫ者어ᄂᆞᆯ今夫娼妓의汙ᄂᆞᆫ貞婦의所羞며奴婢의賤은常人의所惡라此의羞ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄅᆞᆯ彼의行ᄒᆞ기許홈은法의滯홈이오此의惡ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄅᆞᆯ彼에加ᄒᆞ기準홈은法의偏홈이니天下人이其可홈을同ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者아닌則其不可홈은自然ᄒᆞ야一則其惡風을流播ᄒᆞ야人世의面目을穢ᄒᆞ고一則王者의民을私有ᄒᆞ야國家의大權을竊홈인故로文明ᄒᆞᆫ軌度가漸廣홈을隨ᄒᆞ야法의改正ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ步趨가亦進ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니蓋自由ᄂᆞᆫ良惡의分別이有ᄒᆞ야天理의正直홈을遵ᄒᆞᆫ則良自由며人慾의邪僻홈을任ᄒᆞᆫ則惡自由라謂ᄒᆞ고通義ᄂᆞᆫ眞假의區劃이存ᄒᆞ야眞通義ᄂᆞᆫ天然ᄒᆞᆫ良自由ᄅᆞᆯ守ᄒᆞ고假通義ᄂᆞᆫ人爲ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ惡自由ᄅᆞᆯ恣ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로法律이其良惡眞假의辨을立ᄒᆞ야人生權利의大病을醫治ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ金丹이라
paragraphs.modern: 此로 由하여 觀하건대 人生의 諸般權利가 雖其天生의 備具한 者나 人爲한 法律의 關係로 其分度의 增減이 有한지라 天授한 權利를 人力으로 操縱하기 不可하다 하여 其自便을 任寘할진대 放蕩한 弊俗과 壤亂한 惡習이 日로 增하며 月로 加하여 其涯涘의 浩大함이 測度하기 不能하리니 四端과 五倫의 綱紀와 秩序를 依憑하여 法律의 禁防이 極密한 制를 設하며 至愼한 規를 立하여도 猶且其千岐萬條의 絲棼毫細한 橫恣性과 放縱心은 鋤除하기 不盡하며 剪滅하기 甚難하여 娼妓의 淫을 賣함은 自己가 自己의 心으로 禽獸의 自由를 行함이오 奴婢의 世로 傳함은 他人이 他人의 身에 蠻夷의 通義를 存함이로되 習俗의 浸潤으로 人世의 常事를 狃成하여 法律의 公正한 道理와 威力으로도 抑遏하는 功을 難期하니 如此한 弊風惡俗도 各其人의 權利라 謂함이 可할가 否라 凡事를 行하여 其心에 可한 者는 天下人이 皆曰可라 할지며 行하여 其心에 不可한 者는 天下人이 亦皆曰不可라 할지니 大抵人의 自由와 通義는 天下人의 普同한 權利라 然한 故로 一人의 可不可가 天下人의 同然한 者어늘 今夫娼妓의 汙는 貞婦의 所羞며 奴婢의 賤은 常人의 所惡라 此의 羞하는 者를 彼의 行하기 許함은 法의 滯함이오 此의 惡하는 者를 彼에 加하기 準함은 法의 偏함이니 天下人이 其可함을 同하는 者아닌 則其不可함은 自然하여 一則其惡風을 流播하여 人世의 面目을 穢하고 一則王者의 民을 私有하여 國家의 大權을 竊함인 故로 文明한 軌度가 漸廣함을 隨하여 法의 改正하는 步趨가 亦進하나니 蓋自由는 良惡의 分別이 有하여 天理의 正直함을 遵한 則良自由며 人慾의 邪僻함을 任한 則惡自由라 謂하고 通義는 眞假의 區劃이 存하여 眞通義는 天然한 良自由를 守하고 假通義는 人爲하는 惡自由를 恣하는 故로 法律이 其良惡眞假의 辨을 立하여 人生權利의 大病을 醫治하는 金丹이라
paragraphs.en: Viewed from this, though the various rights of human life are all endowed at birth, the measure of them increases or decreases in connection with man-made law. If, on the plea that heaven-bestowed rights may not be controlled by human power, they are left to each person's convenience, dissolute customs and disorderly evil habits will increase day by day and month by month and their boundless extent will be impossible to fathom; even if, relying on the order and discipline of the four sprouts and five human relations, law sets up the most tightly guarded restrictions and the most cautious rules, still the tangled threads of its thousand branches and ten thousand clauses, the reckless nature and the unbridled heart, cannot be weeded out entirely and are very hard to cut away. The selling of lewdness by prostitutes is a person exercising the liberty of beasts by her own heart; the hereditary passing of slaves is one person keeping barbarian rightful claims over another's body. Yet, with custom's gradual seeping in, these have become ordinary things of the human world, and even the just principles and authority of the law can hardly be expected to succeed in suppressing them. Can such bad customs and evil habits be called each person's rights? No. Whatever a man does that his own heart finds acceptable, all under heaven will say is acceptable; and whatever a man does that his own heart finds unacceptable, all under heaven will also say is unacceptable. Since a person's liberty and rightful claims are rights common to all under heaven, one man's acceptable and unacceptable are the same as all men's. Now the foulness of prostitution is a shame to the chaste wife, and the baseness of slavery is hated by ordinary people. To allow the other to do what this one is ashamed of is the law's stagnation, and to permit the other to inflict on this one what he hates is the law's partiality; since it is not that all under heaven share in finding it acceptable, its unacceptability is natural: the one spreads evil customs and fouls the face of the human world, and the other privately possesses the king's people and usurps the great authority of the state. Therefore, as the standards of civilization gradually widen, the pace of reform of the law also advances. For liberty has a distinction of good and bad: if it follows the rightness of heaven's principle it is called good liberty, and if it indulges the depravity of human desire it is called bad liberty; and rightful claims have a division of true and false: true rightful claims keep natural good liberty, and false rightful claims give free rein to man-made bad liberty. Therefore the law, establishing the distinction of good and bad, true and false, is the elixir that cures the great sickness of human rights.

paragraphs.orig: 人民의敎育이不足ᄒᆞᆫ則其自由의良惡과通義의眞假ᄅᆞᆯ不解ᄒᆞ야其權利ᄅᆞᆯ誤用ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ故로或自己의軌轍을讓退ᄒᆞ며或他人의境域을蹂躪ᄒᆞ야恬然히常度ᄅᆞᆯ作ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니是以로人民의權利ᄅᆞᆯ欲平ᄒᆞᆯ딘ᄃᆡ敎育을先務ᄒᆞ야人人으로各守ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ知識이有ᄒᆞ게홈이政治의大道라邦國을固守ᄒᆞ야其權利ᄅᆞᆯ保有ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者ᄂᆞᆫ其國人의各人權利ᄅᆞᆯ善護홈이可ᄒᆞ니千萬人의集合홈으로一國의大ᄅᆞᆯ成ᄒᆞᆫ則此ᄂᆞᆫ衆流ᄅᆞᆯ受ᄒᆞ야滄海의浩大홈이오土壤을積ᄒᆞ야山岳의崇高홈이라一人權利의難奪이一國權利의難犯과同ᄒᆞ거ᄂᆞᆯ若國中의人民이其相與ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ際에强者가弱者ᄅᆞᆯ是侮ᄒᆞ며貴者가賤者ᄅᆞᆯ是慢ᄒᆞ면强國과弱國의不敵홈도理勢의自然이라ᄒᆞ야强國이弱國의權利ᄅᆞᆯ侵越ᄒᆞ야도其人民이當然ᄒᆞᆫ道로視ᄒᆞ고些少의憤怒도不激ᄒᆞᆯ디라然則人民이各其自己權利의貴重홈을愛ᄒᆞᆫ然後에其國權利의貴重홈도亦知ᄒᆞ야死守ᄒᆞ기ᄅᆞᆯ誓ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니此ᄂᆞᆫ敎育으로開導ᄒᆞ야其實效ᄅᆞᆯ奏홈이오法律의保護ᄅᆞᆯ獨任ᄒᆞ야其功을著홈야니라是以로權利ᄂᆞᆫ敎育으로根本을立ᄒᆞ고法律로護衛ᄅᆞᆯ作ᄒᆞ야二者가具備ᄒᆞᆫ然後에完美ᄒᆞᆫ境에始抵ᄒᆞ다謂ᄒᆞᆯ디니開導의功效ᄅᆞᆯ須ᄒᆞ야克就ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ者라
paragraphs.modern: 人民의 敎育이 不足한 則其自由의 良惡과 通義의 眞假를 不解하여 其權利를 誤用하는 故로 或自己의 軌轍을 讓退하며 或他人의 境域을 蹂躪하여 恬然히 常度를 作하나니 是以로 人民의 權利를 欲平할진대 敎育을 先務하여 人人으로 各守하는 知識이 有하게 함이 政治의 大道라 邦國을 固守하여 其權利를 保有하는 者는 其國人의 各人權利를 善護함이 可하니 千萬人의 集合함으로 一國의 大를 成한 則此는 衆流를 受하여 滄海의 浩大함이오 土壤을 積하여 山岳의 崇高함이라 一人權利의 難奪이 一國權利의 難犯과 同하거늘 若國中의 人民이 其相與하는 際에 强者가 弱者를 是侮하며 貴者가 賤者를 是慢하면 强國과 弱國의 不敵함도 理勢의 自然이라 하여 强國이 弱國의 權利를 侵越하여도 其人民이 當然한 道로 視하고 些少의 憤怒도 不激할지라 然則人民이 各其自己權利의 貴重함을 愛한 然後에 其國權利의 貴重함도 亦知하여 死守하기를 誓하나니 此는 敎育으로 開導하여 其實效를 奏함이오 法律의 保護를 獨任하여 其功을 著함 아니라 是以로 權利는 敎育으로 根本을 立하고 法律로 護衛를 作하여 二者가 具備한 然後에 完美한 境에 始抵하다 謂할지니 開導의 功效를 須하여 克就하는 者라
paragraphs.en: If the people's education is insufficient, they do not understand the good and bad of liberty or the true and false of rightful claims, and misuse their rights, so that some yield the tracks they should keep, or trample on others' territory and calmly make it their regular course. Therefore if one wishes to level people's rights, one must first make education the priority, so that every person has the knowledge to keep his own; that is the great way of government. One who firmly guards a country and holds its rights would do well to protect the rights of each of his countrymen: when ten million people are brought together and form a great nation, it is like the vastness of the ocean that receives all the streams, and the loftiness of the mountains that heap up the soil. The impossibility of taking away one man's rights is the same as the impossibility of violating the rights of a whole nation; but if, in their dealings with one another, the people of a country let the strong insult the weak and the noble be arrogant to the humble, then people will say that the non-equality of strong and weak countries is the natural way of things, and even if a strong country encroaches on the rights of a weak country they will regard it as proper and not be roused to the slightest anger. Hence only after the people love the preciousness of their own rights do they also know the preciousness of their nation's rights and swear to defend them to the death. This is the real result achieved by guiding with education, and not an achievement won by relying on the protection of law alone. Therefore rights are founded on education and guarded by law, and only when both are present may we say that the perfect state is first reached; it is something achieved only by relying on the efficacy of guidance.
